41	## Runtime State
42	
43	By default, deadreckon writes runtime state to:
44	
45	```bash
46	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon
47	```
48	
49	For disposable tests, set:
50	
51	```bash
52	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
53	```
54	
55	Per-run artifacts include:
56	
57	```text
58	state.json
59	history.json
60	events.jsonl
61	traces.jsonl
62	spend.jsonl
63	provenance.jsonl
64	snapshots/turn-<N>/
65	proofs/turn-acceptance.json
66	working/ or library/<scope>/<run-id>/
67	```
68	
69	Completed accepted runs are promoted to:
70	
71	```bash
72	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/
73	```
74	
75	The directory where you launch `deadreckon run` is recorded as `launch-dir`.
76	In a git repo, the normal default is a separate worktree on a `dr/...` branch.
77	Your checkout is left unchanged until `deadreckon apply <run-id>`.
78	
79	## First Run
80	
81	Interactive setup:
82	
83	```bash
84	deadreckon init
85	deadreckon doctor
86	```
87	
88	Non-interactive examples:
89	
90	```bash
91	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
92	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
93	deadreckon init --provider openai --api-key "$OPENAI_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
94	```
95	
96	Inspect or edit config:
97	
98	```bash
99	deadreckon config get defaults.provider
100	deadreckon config provider
101	deadreckon config provider cli:codex
102	deadreckon config model
103	deadreckon config model gpt-5.1-codex --provider cli:codex
104	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
105	deadreckon config set defaults.sandbox auto
106	deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
107	```
108	
109	## Keyless Smoke Run
110	
111	Use this to prove the harness works without provider keys:
112	
113	```bash
114	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
115	rm -rf "$DEADRECKON_HOME"
116	
117	deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
118	deadreckon list
119	deadreckon status
120	```
121	
122	The default list is compact, project-scoped, and shows eight-character run IDs.
123	Commands accept unique prefixes, so `deadreckon show 861c51bf` works when that
124	prefix is unique. Most run-id arguments also accept `latest` or `last`, resolved
125	to the latest run for the current project. Use `--all` for global history and
126	`show` when you need full paths, IDs, traces, docs, and next actions.
127	
128	Inspect the latest run:
129	
130	```bash
131	deadreckon show latest
132	```
133	
134	Then attach to or finish it:
135	
136	```bash
137	deadreckon attach latest
138	```
139	
140	## Normal Coding Run
141	
142	After `init`, the normal path in a git repo is:
143	
144	```bash
145	deadreckon run "make a full task productivity tracker in nodejs that allows me to manage my day"
146	deadreckon attach latest
147	deadreckon status
148	deadreckon finish latest
149	deadreckon apply latest --autostash --cleanup
150	```
151	
152	`run` prints the run id and attach command as soon as state is created:
153	
154	```text
155	started run <short-id> (<full-id>)
156	attach: deadreckon attach <short-id>
157	```
158	
159	Before it creates state or files, `run` prints a preview. In a clean git repo,
160	the preview shows `mode: worktree`, the `dr/...` branch, the base ref, and the
161	worktree path. Use `--yes` to skip the confirmation in scripts or `--preview`
162	to print the block and exit.
163	
164	Mode overrides:
165	
166	```bash
167	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh                         # old empty working dir
168	deadreckon run "goal" --from .                        # gitignore-aware copy
169	deadreckon run "goal" --worktree                      # force git worktree
170	deadreckon run "goal" --base main --branch dr/my-task # customize worktree branch
171	deadreckon run "goal" --allow-dirty                   # seed dirty files into worktree
172	deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot   # edit current dir directly
173	```
174	
175	Outside git, interactive `run` offers git init, copy mode, or cancel.
176	Non-interactive runs outside git need an explicit mode:
177	
178	```bash
179	deadreckon run "goal" --from . --yes
180	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh --yes
181	git init && deadreckon run "goal" --yes
182	```
183	
184	The default config from `deadreckon init` supplies the provider, sandbox, `$10` spend cap, and `3600` second wall-clock cap. Use flags only when overriding those defaults:
185	
186	```bash
187	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex
188	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
189	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code
190	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code --model sonnet
191	deadreckon run "goal" --provider anthropic
192	deadreckon run "goal" --provider openai
193	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox sandbox-exec
194	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox none
195	deadreckon run "goal" --max-spend 5
196	deadreckon run "goal" --max-wall-seconds 1800
197	```
198	
199	`deadreckon run --preview "goal"` prints the provider and model before creating
200	state. `--model` is per-run; `deadreckon config model ...` makes the model
201	default for that provider. For CLI providers, `provider default` means
202	deadreckon delegates model choice to Codex or Claude Code unless you pass
203	`--model`.
204	
205	Run docs use their own provider route. By default deadreckon uses
206	`defaults.doc_provider`, then an installed subscription CLI (`cli:codex` before
207	`cli:claude-code`), then the run provider. Override it per run when needed:
208	
209	```bash
210	deadreckon run "goal" --doc-provider cli:codex
211	deadreckon config set defaults.doc_provider cli:codex
212	```
213	
214	Spend above `$50` requires confirmation:
215	
216	```bash
217	deadreckon run "large goal" --max-spend 75 --i-know-its-a-lot
218	```
219	
220	## TUI
221	
222	Open the dashboard:
223	
224	```bash
225	deadreckon attach <run-id>
226	```
227	
228	The TUI shows:
229	
230	```text
231	run id, status, phase, goal
232	working directory
233	per-turn timer
234	compact spend/context telemetry
235	wide center-left tool-call/provider activity stream
236	narrow center-right live files being generated
237	bottom supervised process/status panel
238	completed-run Markdown docs view
239	provider activity from live Codex session logs
240	```
241	
242	Keys:
243	
244	```text
245	Ctrl-D   detach without killing the run
246	q        quit
247	Esc      quit
248	Tab      move focus between panels
249	j/k      scroll focused panel
250	PgUp/PgDn scroll focused panel by a page
251	```
252	
253	After a run completes, the TUI footer adds lifecycle actions:
254	
255	```text
256	a        apply a completed worktree run
257	b        abandon/discard a completed worktree run
258	d        toggle formatted RUN-NARRATIVE.md docs in the main panel
259	m        materialize/export a completed copy/fresh artifact
260	e        extend a completed copy/fresh run with a follow-up goal
261	s        show run details
262	```
263	
264	The docs view uses a Markdown parser and ratatui styles for headings, bullets,
265	inline code, fenced code blocks, links, horizontal rules, and task lists. Press
266	`d` again to return to provider activity. Scroll it with the same `j/k`,
267	arrow-key, page-key, and mouse-wheel bindings.
268	
269	## Generated Docs
270	
271	Every run writes `.deadreckon/docs/_incremental.jsonl` at turn boundaries and
272	emits a `docs_checkpoint` event. Completion then runs the doc polish step unless
273	you passed `--no-docs`.
274	
275	```bash
276	deadreckon doc latest
277	deadreckon doc latest --kind as-built
278	deadreckon doc latest --kind decisions
279	deadreckon doc latest --polish --force
280	deadreckon doc latest --polish --doc-provider cli:codex --budget-cap 0.25
281	```
282	
283	The polish preview lists the provider, why it was selected, the four narrator
284	subskills, token budget, budget cap, and inputs hash. `--no-confirm` skips the
285	prompt for scripts. Results are recorded in `polish.json` with one status line
286	per subskill.
287	
288	The TUI does not start, kill, resume, or undo runs. Use CLI commands for those controls.
289	
290	## Completion Actions
291	
292	Completed `run` and `extend` commands show the same lifecycle actions in the CLI:
293	
294	```text
295	completed action [a apply, b abandon, d docs, s show, q quit]:
296	completed action [m materialize, e extend, d docs, s show, q quit]:
297	```
298	
299	Worktree runs use `a` to squash-apply changes to the current branch or `b` to
300	discard the worktree and temporary branch. Copy/fresh runs use `m` to copy the
301	library artifact into a normal directory, `e` to start a child run from the
302	completed artifact, `d` to read `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, or `s` to inspect state and lineage. Pass `--no-hints` to
303	`run` or `attach` when scripting.
304	
305	The CLI aliases use friendlier lifecycle names:
306	
307	```bash
308	deadreckon finish latest                            # choose apply or export from run mode
309	deadreckon done "builds and passes tests"           # write done criteria
310	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project   # alias for materialize
311	deadreckon keep latest --autostash --cleanup         # alias for apply
312	deadreckon discard latest                            # alias for abandon
313	deadreckon next                                      # alias for status
314	deadreckon watch latest                              # alias for attach
315	deadreckon stop latest                               # alias for kill
316	deadreckon continue latest                           # alias for resume
317	deadreckon inspect latest                            # alias for show
318	deadreckon docs latest                               # alias for doc
319	deadreckon prune --completed                         # alias for cleanup
320	```
321	
322	`extend` is still available for completed worktree runs from the CLI. It creates
323	a new `dr/...` branch from the parent run's branch, so the follow-up keeps the
324	parent changes without applying them to your checkout first:
325	
326	```bash
327	deadreckon extend <worktree-run-id> "continue with the next change"
328	```
329	
330	## List, Show, Kill, Resume
331	
332	```bash
333	deadreckon list
334	deadreckon list --all
335	deadreckon status
336	deadreckon next
337	deadreckon show <run-id>
338	deadreckon show latest
339	deadreckon inspect latest
340	deadreckon finish latest
341	deadreckon finish latest --dest ./finished-project
342	deadreckon finish latest --autostash --cleanup
343	deadreckon apply <run-id>
344	deadreckon apply <run-id> --autostash
345	deadreckon apply <run-id> --cleanup --no-confirm
346	deadreckon apply <run-id> --strategy merge
347	deadreckon apply <run-id> --strategy cherry-pick --no-confirm
348	deadreckon keep <run-id> --autostash --cleanup
349	deadreckon abandon <run-id>
350	deadreckon discard <run-id>
351	deadreckon abandon <run-id> --keep-branch
352	deadreckon cleanup --completed
353	deadreckon cleanup --stale --force
354	deadreckon cleanup --all --completed --no-confirm
355	deadreckon prune --completed
356	deadreckon kill <run-id>
357	deadreckon stop <run-id>
358	deadreckon kill <run-id> --force
359	deadreckon resume <run-id>
360	deadreckon continue <run-id>
361	deadreckon resume <run-id> --from-turn 2
362	deadreckon resume <run-id> --max-wall-seconds 3600
363	```
364	
365	`finish` is the easiest completion command. For a worktree run it routes to
366	`apply`; for a fresh/copy run it routes to `export`; for an in-place run it
367	prints review, docs, and undo guidance.
368	
369	Re-running `deadreckon apply <run-id>` after the changes are already on the
370	target branch is safe: deadreckon reports `already applied` instead of creating
371	or failing an empty commit. Add `--cleanup` to remove the temporary worktree and
372	branch in that already-applied state.
373	
374	`resume --from-turn N` truncates reconstructed history to turn `N` and continues with turn `N + 1`.
375	
376	## Undo
377	
378	Restore the previous turn snapshot:
379	
380	```bash
381	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
382	```
383	
384	Restore a specific turn:
385	
386	```bash
387	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 1
388	```
389	
390	Undo restores the run working directory from `snapshots/turn-<N>/` and records
391	an undo trace. For in-place runs, undo restores the original source path because
392	the agent edited that directory directly.
393	
394	## Done Criteria
395	
396	If a run has no custom acceptance spec, `dr-gate` checks that the working directory exists and runs `cargo test` when `Cargo.toml` is present.
397	
398	The normal path is English first:
399	
400	```bash
401	deadreckon done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
402	deadreckon done add "users can save drawings"
403	deadreckon done check
404	deadreckon run "goal"
405	```
406	
407	`done` asks the configured provider to convert plain-English criteria into `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`. Short pack names are available without a provider when they fit:
408	
409	```bash
410	deadreckon done add build
411	deadreckon done add node
412	deadreckon done add static-site
413	deadreckon done add browser
414	deadreckon done add playwright
415	deadreckon done add vite
416	deadreckon done add nextjs
417	deadreckon done add python
418	```
419	
420	Runs and chains prompt before starting when no project acceptance file exists. Helper scripts generated by packs or drafts live under `.deadreckon/acceptance/` and are copied into the run workspace before `dr-gate` executes.
421	
422	The compiled YAML looks like this:
423	
424	```yaml
425	name: notes check
426	checks:
427	  - kind: file_exists
428	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
429	  - kind: content_match
430	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
431	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
432	  - kind: build_success
433	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
434	```
435	
436	Supported check kinds:
437	
438	```text
439	cargo_test
440	file_exists
441	content_match
442	build_success
443	shell
444	```
445	
446	`content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text. Shell, build, and cargo checks record duration plus clipped stdout/stderr so failures are readable.
447	
448	The acceptance marker is signed with a run-local nonce. A marker written by the agent is refused.

43	## 1. System Overview & Mental Model
44	
45	deadreckon is a Rust 2024 CLI harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**: `deadreckon run <goal>` creates durable run state, picks a BYOK provider route, executes turns inside a platform-native sandbox, writes spend/provenance/trace records after every turn, and exits only when the LLM declares done, a budget caps the run, or the operator kills it. The CLI is the user-facing layer; `deadreckon-runtime` owns orchestration across providers, sandboxes, docs, and promotion; `deadreckon-core` owns deterministic primitives and durable schemas.
46	
47	```
48	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
49	│ USER                                                                      │
50	│ deadreckon run "make a hello-world Rust binary" --max-spend 5             │
51	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
52	                                 │
53	┌────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────┐
54	│ CLI LAYER (crates/deadreckon)                                             │
55	│   cli.rs       clap parser definitions                                    │
56	│   main.rs      command handlers, ratatui rendering, post-run summary       │
57	└────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┘
58	                                 │ create_run → acquire_lock → runtime loop
59	                                 ▼
60	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
61	│ RUNTIME ORCHESTRATION (crates/deadreckon-runtime)                         │
62	│                                                                           │
63	│  turn_loop.rs  provider turns, sandboxed tool dispatch, cancellation,      │
64	│                acceptance gate invocation, promotion orchestration         │
65	│  polish.rs     optional end-of-run doc polish via a doc-provider           │
66	└──┬──────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────┬────────────────┘
67	   │ durable primitives       │ ProviderRouter::complete  │ run_sandbox
68	   ▼                          ▼                          ▼
69	┌──────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────┐
70	│ CORE LIBRARY             │  │ PROVIDERS            │  │ SANDBOX              │
71	│ state, paths, locks      │  │ HTTP: anthropic,     │  │ sandbox-exec, bwrap, │
72	│ artifacts, docs, events  │  │ openai, compatible   │  │ docker, none, auto   │
73	│ gate, promotion, chains  │  │ CLI: claude, codex   │  │ policy, PID/cancel   │
74	│ adapter-free schemas     │  │ TEST: smoke          │  │ doctor checks        │
75	└────────────┬─────────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘  └──────────┬───────────┘
76	             │                           │                         │
77	             └───────────────────────────┴─────────────┬───────────┘
78	                                                       ▼
79	┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
80	│ RUNTIME STATE (~/.deadreckon/)                                            │
81	│ runstate/<scope>/runs/<run-id>, library/<scope>/<run-id>, locks, config   │
82	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
83	```
84	
85	Why this shape works:
86	
87	- **The CLI is thin.** It parses args, sets up state, hands off to `deadreckon-runtime`, and prints summaries. Durable schemas and atomic file operations live in `deadreckon-core`.
88	- **State is on disk before every meaningful change.** `state.json` is atomic-written via temp+rename after every phase transition, snapshot, spend record, and tool call.
89	- **The agent cannot mark its own gate.** `dr-gate` is a separate binary that signs an acceptance marker against a nonce only it can read; the deadreckon binary refuses to mark a run `Completed` without that signed marker.
90	- **Sandboxes are platform-native.** macOS uses Seatbelt; Linux uses Bubblewrap; Docker is opt-in. No daemon, no `bollard`, no Lima.
91	- **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** Subscription-bearing users drive deadreckon by routing turns through their local `claude` or `codex` CLIs; no API key required.
92

194	
195	## 3. The Two-Layer Architecture
196	
197	deadreckon mirrors the Printing Press split (AS-BUILT §3):
198	
199	| Layer | Owns | Lives in | Language |
200	|---|---|---|---|
201	| **Skill** | Agent-facing prose, judgment, prompt frame | `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md` | Markdown |
202	| **Binary** | State, locks, sandboxes, providers, gates | `crates/deadreckon*` | Rust |
203	
204	The skill is invoked indirectly: it sits at the path recorded in `state.skill_path` and is read into the prompt frame by `build_prompt` in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`. The binary never reaches into skill internals. New skills can be added under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and selected with `deadreckon run --skill <name>`.
205	
206	This split lets each side do what it's good at:
207	
208	- The Rust binary enforces invariants — locks, atomic file ops, signed acceptance markers, sandboxed subprocesses.
209	- The Markdown skill makes judgment calls — what to ask the LLM for, what tool sequence to prefer, when to declare done.
210

213	## 4. State Machine & Persistence
214	
215	### 4.1 `PipelineState`
216	
217	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/state.rs:77-110`:
218	
219	```rust
220	pub struct PipelineState {
221	    pub version: u32,                       // STATE_VERSION = 1 (line 15)
222	    pub goal: String,
223	    pub task_key: String,
224	    pub run_id: String,
225	    pub scope: String,
226	    pub status: RunStatus,
227	    pub current_phase_id: PhaseId,
228	    pub started_at: DateTime<Utc>,
229	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
230	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
231	    pub run_root: PathBuf,
232	    pub working_dir: PathBuf,
233	    pub skill_name: String,
234	    pub skill_path: PathBuf,
235	    pub sandbox: String,
236	    pub provider: Option<String>,
237	    pub max_spend_usd: Option<f64>,
238	    pub max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
239	    pub total_spend_usd: f64,
240	    pub total_wall_seconds: f64,
241	    pub turn: u32,
242	    pub pause_reason: Option<String>,
243	    pub failure_reason: Option<String>,
244	    pub child_pids: Vec<u32>,
245	    pub killed_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
246	    pub promoted_library_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
247	    pub phases: Vec<PhaseState>,
248	}
249	```
250	
251	### 4.2 Status and phase enums
252	
253	`state.rs:17-26`:
254	
255	```rust
256	pub enum RunStatus {
257	    Pending, Planned, Executing, Completed, Failed, Killed,
258	}
259	```
260	
261	`state.rs:42-75`:
262	
263	```rust
264	pub struct PhaseId(pub u16);
265	
266	pub struct PhaseState {
267	    pub id: PhaseId,
268	    pub name: String,
269	    pub status: PhaseStatus,    // Pending | Planned | Executing | Completed | Failed
270	    pub plan_path: Option<PathBuf>,
271	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
272	}
273	```
274	
275	### 4.3 Phase numbering (gap-numbered)
276	
277	`state.rs:233-254` initializes seven phases for every new run:
278	
279	| `PhaseId` | name | role |
280	|---|---|---|
281	| 0 | `init` | skill load, run-id mint, working-dir create |
282	| 10 | `plan` | reserved; currently a no-op |
283	| 20 | `provider` | router built from config, fallback chain resolved |
284	| 30 | `sandbox` | sandbox backend selected, profile prepared |
285	| 40 | `execute` | the turn loop runs here; sets `RunStatus::Executing` |
286	| 50 | `verify` | post-loop verification (currently runs `dr-gate`) |
287	| 60 | `complete` | acceptance marker validated, promotion atomic-swaps, `RunStatus::Completed` |
288	
289	The gap-numbering (0, 10, 20 …) leaves room for future phases (e.g., 15, 25, 55) without re-writing on-disk state.
290	
291	### 4.4 Status transitions
292	
293	`state.rs:150-169` is the only function that mutates `PipelineState.status`:
294	
295	```rust
296	pub fn set_phase_status(&mut self, id: PhaseId, status: PhaseStatus) -> Result<()> {
297	    let now = Utc::now();
298	    let phase = self.phases.iter_mut().find(|phase| phase.id == id)
299	        .ok_or_else(|| DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("phase {}", id.0)))?;
300	    phase.status = status;
301	    phase.updated_at = now;
302	    self.current_phase_id = id;
303	    self.updated_at = now;
304	    self.status = match status {
305	        PhaseStatus::Executing => RunStatus::Executing,
306	        PhaseStatus::Failed => RunStatus::Failed,
307	        PhaseStatus::Completed if id == PhaseId(60) => RunStatus::Completed,
308	        PhaseStatus::Planned => RunStatus::Planned,
309	        PhaseStatus::Pending | PhaseStatus::Completed => self.status,
310	    };
311	    Ok(())
312	}
313	```
314	
315	Key rule: `RunStatus::Completed` is reachable **only** through `Phase(60).Completed`, which the loop refuses to set without `validate_acceptance_marker()` passing (§13).
316	
317	### 4.5 Atomic persistence
318	
319	`state.rs:353-373`:
320	
321	```rust
322	pub(crate) fn atomic_write_json<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
323	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(...)?;
324	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
325	    let mut temp = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).with_path(parent)?;
326	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut temp, value).with_json_path(path)?;
327	    temp.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
328	    temp.as_file_mut().sync_all().with_path(path)?;   // fsync before rename
329	    persist_temp(temp, path)
330	}
331	```
332	
333	Every state-changing function ends with `save_state(state)?`. Crashes never leave a half-written `state.json`.
334	
335	JSONL files (`spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`) use `append_json_line` (`state.rs:375-388`): open in append mode, write line + newline, `sync_all`.
336	
337	### 4.6 Schema versioning
338	
339	`STATE_VERSION = 1` (`state.rs:15`) gates future migrations. `load_state` rejects unknown versions; migrations would land here.
340

393	│               ├── child-pids/

395	│               ├── sandbox/       # per-run Seatbelt profile (if mac) or bwrap args

402	├── locks/

404	└── library/
405	    └── <scope>/
406	        └── <run_id>/
407	            ├── manifest.json      # PromotionManifest
408	            └── ...                # promoted working tree
409	```
410	
411	The split between `runstate/` (mutable working state) and `library/` (durable promoted artifacts) is deliberate: `runstate/` is per-scope and ephemeral; `library/` is global and intended to outlive cleanup. The `state.working_dir` field starts pointing at `runstate/.../working/` and is rewritten to `library/<scope>/<run_id>/` after promotion.
412	
413	### 5.3 Path derivation
414	
415	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:9-65` exposes:
416	
417	```rust
418	impl DeadreckonPaths {
419	    pub fn home(&self) -> &Path                              // ~/.deadreckon (or DEADRECKON_HOME)
420	    pub fn config_path(&self) -> PathBuf                     // home/config.toml
421	    pub fn runstate_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                    // home/runstate
422	    pub fn scope_root(&self, scope: &str) -> PathBuf
423	    pub fn current_pointer_path(&self, scope, task_key) -> PathBuf
424	    pub fn run_root(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
425	    pub fn locks_dir(&self) -> PathBuf                       // home/locks
426	    pub fn library_dir(&self, scope, run_id) -> PathBuf
427	}
428	```
429	
430	Scope (`paths.rs:67-86`) derives from `DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT` env var, or the nearest `.git` root, or `cwd`. The literal scope string is `"<sanitized-basename>-<fnv1a32-hex>"` of the canonical path — unique per worktree, stable per checkout.
431	
432	Task key (`paths.rs:88-99`) is `"<slug-of-goal>-<fnv1a32-hex-of-goal>"` (slug capped at 48 chars). Two runs with the same goal share a task key (and a lock).
433	
434	---
435	
436	## 6. Run Lifecycle & Phase Machine
437	
438	Sequence for a typical `deadreckon run` invocation:
439	
440	```
441	main.rs run_command()
442	  ↓
443	  paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover()
444	  ↓
445	  state = create_run(paths, RunOptions{...})       # state.rs:178-231
446	  │   ├── mint run_id (uuid simple form)
447	  │   ├── derive scope (paths.rs:67) and task_key (paths.rs:88)
448	  │   ├── create run_root/working/snapshots/proofs/gate/turns
449	  │   ├── write gate/nonce (uuid)
450	  │   ├── initialize 7 phases (state.rs:233-254)
451	  │   ├── write CurrentRunPointer
452	  │   └── save_state()
453	  ↓
454	  lock = acquire_lock(paths, task_key, run_id, scope, "run", 30min)
455	  │   └── lock.rs:89-158
456	  ↓
457	  state.child_pids = vec![cli_pid]; save_state()
458	  ↓
459	  set_phase_status(20, Completed); save_state()   # provider built
460	  set_phase_status(30, Completed); save_state()   # sandbox resolved
461	  ↓
462	  outcome = run_turn_loop(state, router, RunLoopConfig{...})
463	  ↓
464	  state.child_pids.clear(); save_state()
465	  lock.release()
466	  ↓
467	  match outcome { Done | PausedAtCap | Killed | Failed }
468	  print_run_locations(state)
469	```
470	
471	`Completed` is only reached if the turn loop emits `RunLoopOutcome::Done`, which itself requires:
472	
473	1. The loop saw `Action::Done` (or a CLI sub-agent finished with file changes), **and**
474	2. `run_acceptance_gate(state)` succeeded (invoked the external `dr-gate` binary), **and**
475	3. `validate_acceptance_marker(state)` succeeded (signature + run_id check), **and**
476	4. `promote_if_ready(state)` swapped `working/` → `library/<scope>/<run_id>/`, **and**
477	5. `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)` ran (which is the only path to `RunStatus::Completed`).
478	
479	---
480	
481	## 7. Locks, Heartbeats, Crash Recovery
482	
483	### 7.1 `LockState`
484	
485	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/lock.rs:15-24`:
486	
487	```rust
488	pub struct LockState {
489	    pub task_key: String,
490	    pub run_id: String,
491	    pub scope: String,
492	    pub phase: String,
493	    pub pid: u32,
494	    pub acquired_at: DateTime<Utc>,
495	    pub updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
496	}
497	```
498	
499	Lock file lives at `~/.deadreckon/locks/<scope>--<task_key>.lock` (`lock.rs:86`).
500	
501	### 7.2 Acquisition
502	
503	`lock.rs:89-158`:
504	
505	1. Create the `.lock` file.
506	2. `fs2::FileExt::try_lock_exclusive` for OS-level advisory lock.
507	3. If `EWOULDBLOCK`, read existing `LockState` from disk. If owner matches **or** lock is stale, proceed. Otherwise refuse.
508	4. Stale detection: `acquired_at` age > `DEFAULT_STALE_AFTER` (30 min, `lock.rs:13`) **or** `pid_is_alive(pid)` returns false. PID liveness is `nix::sys::signal::kill(pid, 0)` (`lock.rs:235-245`): `ESRCH` → dead, anything else → alive.
509	5. Write the new `LockState` to disk.
510	6. Return a `LockGuard` that releases on drop.
511	
512	### 7.3 Heartbeat
513	
514	`lock.rs:47-51`:
515	
516	```rust
517	pub fn heartbeat(&mut self, phase: impl Into<String>) -> Result<()> {
518	    self.state.phase = phase.into();
519	    self.state.updated_at = Utc::now();
520	    write_lock_state_to_file(&mut self.file, &self.path, &self.state)
521	}
522	```
523	
524	Updates `updated_at` to keep stale-detection at bay. Callers in the turn loop tag the current sub-phase (e.g., `"executing-turn-3"`).
525	
526	### 7.4 Release
527	
528	`lock.rs:53-76`. Drops the file lock, deletes the lock file, gracefully handles `NotFound`.
529	
530	### 7.5 Crash recovery
531	
532	If the process holding the lock dies, the lock file persists but `pid_is_alive(pid)` will return false. The next caller sees the stale state and reclaims it. The new caller writes its own PID; previous run state survives intact in `runstate/<scope>/runs/<dead_run_id>/`.
533	
534	---
535	
536	## 8. Atomic Promotion & the Library
537	
538	### 8.1 `PromotionManifest`
539	
540	`crates/deadreckon-core/src/promotion.rs:14-23`:
541	
542	```rust
543	pub struct PromotionManifest {
544	    pub schema_version: u32,
545	    pub run_id: String,
546	    pub scope: String,
547	    pub goal: String,
548	    pub promoted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
549	    pub source_working_dir: PathBuf,
550	    pub provenance_hash: String,   // hash of provenance.jsonl bytes
551	}
552	```
553	
554	### 8.2 Promotion flow
555	
556	`promotion.rs:25-63`:
557	
558	1. **Guard.** `validate_acceptance_marker(state)?` — refuses if marker missing / wrong run_id / unsigned.
559	2. **Recovery.** `recover_promotion()` — idempotent if a previous attempt half-completed (§8.4).
560	3. **Idempotency check.** If `library/<scope>/<run_id>/manifest.json` already exists, update state and return — no work to do.
561	4. **Staging.** Create `library/<scope>/.{run_id}.promoting/` (parent dir created if needed).
562	5. **Move.** `fs::rename(working_dir, staging)` — atomic on same filesystem.
563	6. **Manifest.** Write `manifest.json` inside staging.
564	7. **Final rename.** `fs::rename(staging, library/<scope>/<run_id>/)` — atomic.
565	8. **State update.** `state.working_dir = library_dir`; `state.promoted_library_dir = Some(library_dir)`; `save_state()`.
566	
567	### 8.3 Where promotion happens
568	
569	In `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`, **before** `set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), Completed)`. If promotion fails, the run never reaches `Completed`. The `working/` directory is the source of truth until promotion; after promotion, the library copy is canonical and `working/` is gone.
570	
571	### 8.4 Crash recovery between rename steps
572	
573	`promotion.rs:65-84` handles the half-completed states:
574	
575	- If `staging` exists and final dir doesn't: complete the rename.
576	- If both exist: the final rename happened but didn't atomically remove staging; clean up staging.
577	- If final dir exists but its `manifest.json` is missing: write the manifest.
578	
579	This makes promotion crash-safe across a `kill -9` between the two renames.
580	
581	---
582	
583	## 9. The Turn Loop
584	
585	The load-bearing function lives in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`.
586	
587	### 9.1 `RunLoopConfig`
588	
589	`crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` defines:
590	
591	```rust
592	pub struct RunLoopConfig {
593	    pub provider: Option<String>,
594	    pub max_spend_usd: Option<f64>,
595	    pub max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
596	    pub sandbox_backend: SandboxBackend,
597	    pub max_turns: u32,             // hard cap, currently 12
598	    pub from_turn: Option<u32>,     // resume override
599	    pub event_sender: Option<broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
600	    pub cancellation_token: Option<CancellationToken>,
601	}
602	```
603	
604	### 9.2 Top-level signature
605	
606	The top-level signature is:
607	
608	```rust
609	pub async fn run_turn_loop(
610	    state: &mut PipelineState,
611	    router: &ProviderRouter,
612	    config: RunLoopConfig,
613	) -> Result<RunLoopOutcome>
614	```
615	
616	### 9.3 Loop body (paraphrased; see `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs`)
617	
618	```text
619	load_or_reconstruct_history()      # lines 69, 550-631
620	set Phase(40)=Executing            # line 70
621	save_state(); save_history()       # line 71
622	
623	for turn in (state.turn+1)..=max_turns:
624	    if cancelled or status=Killed:
625	        return Killed
626	    emit TurnStarted event
627	    snapshot_working(turn-1)        # capture pre-turn state
628	    prompt = build_prompt(state, history) [or build_cli_subagent_prompt]
629	    request = ProviderRequest{
630	        prompt, max_output_tokens=2048, cwd, output_path, sandbox_backend,
631	        pid_file=run_root/child-pids/provider-turn-N.pid,
632	        cancellation_token=turn_token,
633	    }
634	    response = router.complete(&request).await
635	    append_trace(llm.complete, latency, response.trace)
636	    state.total_spend_usd += response.spend.cost_usd
637	    state.total_wall_seconds += response.spend.wall_time_seconds
638	    append_spend(...)
639	    if max_spend exceeded: return PausedAtCap
640	    if subscription and max_wall_seconds exceeded: return PausedAtCap
641	
642	    if response is cli_subagent:
643	        changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(turn-1)
644	        if changed.is_empty: return Failed
645	        snapshot_working(turn)
646	        append_trace(tool.cli_subagent, files=changed)
647	        append_provenance_for_files(turn, tool_call_id, model, changed)
648	        run_acceptance_gate(state)        # dr-gate
649	        validate_acceptance_marker(state) # signed?
650	        promote_if_ready(state)           # working → library
651	        set Phase(60)=Completed
652	        return Done
653	
654	    parse Action from response.content (serde tag="action"):
655	        Bash { tool_call_id, command } =>
656	            run_sandbox(SandboxSpec{
657	                program=sh, args=[-lc, command], cwd=working_dir,
658	                pid_file, cancellation_token=turn_token.child_token(),
659	                read_allowlist=[working_dir],
660	                allow_network=false,
661	            }).await
662	            append_trace(tool.bash, stdout, stderr, status)
663	            snapshot_working(turn); append_provenance(turn, changed_files)
664	            history.push("tool {id} result: status={...}")
665	        WriteFile { tool_call_id, path, content } =>
666	            safe_working_path(path); write_file
667	            append_trace(tool.write_file); snapshot_working(turn)
668	            append_provenance(turn, [path])
669	            history.push("tool {id} result: wrote file")
670	        Done { summary } =>
671	            run_acceptance_gate; validate_marker; promote_if_ready
672	            set Phase(60)=Completed
673	            return Done
674	
675	    state.turn = turn; save_history(); save_state()
676	
677	# loop exited via max_turns
678	state.failure_reason = Some("max turn budget exhausted")
679	set Phase(40)=Failed; save_state()
680	return Failed
681	```
682	
683	### 9.4 Action enum
684	
685	Inline in `crates/deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs` (paraphrased):
686	
687	```rust
688	#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
689	#[serde(tag = "action", rename_all = "snake_case")]
690	enum Action {
691	    Bash { tool_call_id: String, command: String },
692	    WriteFile { tool_call_id: String, path: PathBuf, content: String },
693	    Done { summary: Option<String> },
694	}
695	```
696	
697	Providers return JSON; the loop parses one action per turn. The CLI sub-agent path is detected by `response.trace["kind"] == "cli_subagent"` before action parsing — those providers do their own tool calls inside the subprocess and return a narrative, not an action JSON.
698	
699	### 9.5 No smoke fallback in the default path
700	
701	`grep -r "coding_turn_script\|hardcoded_smoke" /Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/` returns empty. The deterministic-script path lives entirely inside `ScriptedSmokeProvider` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/smoke.rs`), reachable only via `deadreckon run --smoke` (which selects the `smoke` provider, not via a bypass of the run loop).
702	
703	### 9.6 Error handling
704	
705	The loop does **not** retry on errors:
706	
707	- Provider error → propagates and the run fails.
708	- Tool-call non-zero exit → result fed back to history, next turn's prompt sees the failure; the model decides whether to retry.
709	- Acceptance failure → run fails; no auto-retry.
710	
711	The bound is `max_turns` (currently 12), not an error budget.
712

715	## 10. Provider Model
716	
717	### 10.1 The `Provider` trait
718	
719	`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/types.rs`:
720	
721	```rust
722	pub trait Provider: Send + Sync {
723	    fn name(&self) -> &str;
724	    fn kind(&self) -> ProviderKind;
725	    fn model(&self) -> &str;
726	    fn has_credential(&self) -> bool;
727	    fn estimate_spend(&self, usage: ProviderUsage) -> SpendEstimate;
728	    fn complete<'a>(&'a self, request: &'a ProviderRequest) -> ProviderFuture<'a>;
729	}
730	```
731	
732	`ProviderRequest` (`lib.rs:83-91`) carries: `prompt`, `max_output_tokens`, optional `cwd`, optional `output_path`, optional `sandbox_backend`, optional `pid_file`, optional `cancellation_token`.
733	
734	`ProviderResponse` (`lib.rs:94-102`) carries: `provider`, `model`, `content`, `usage`, `spend`, `trace` (JSON value).
735	
736	### 10.2 Kinds
737	
738	`lib.rs:52-61`:
739	
740	```rust
741	pub enum ProviderKind {
742	    Anthropic,
743	    OpenAi,
744	    OpenAiCompatible,
745	    CliClaudeCode,
746	    CliCodex,
747	    ScriptedSmoke,
748	}
749	```
750	
751	### 10.3 HTTP adapters
752	
753	A single `ProviderAdapter` (`lib.rs:135-323`) handles all three HTTP kinds via shared `reqwest::Client`:
754	
755	| Kind | Endpoint | Auth header | Default model |
756	|---|---|---|---|
757	| Anthropic | `{base_url}/v1/messages` | `x-api-key: <key>` + `anthropic-version: 2023-06-01` | `claude-sonnet-4-5` |
758	| OpenAI | `{base_url}/chat/completions` | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | configurable |
759	| OpenAI-compatible | `{base_url}/chat/completions` | `Authorization: Bearer <key>` | configurable |
760	
761	Pricing defaults (`lib.rs:531-617`): Anthropic $3/$15 per million in/out; OpenAI $1.25/$10 per million; OpenAI-compatible $0/$0 (user-configured).
762	
763	Response parsing: `parse_anthropic_response` (`lib.rs:688-705`) extracts `content[0].text` + `usage.{input_tokens, output_tokens}`; `parse_openai_response` (`lib.rs:669-686`) extracts `choices[0].message.content` + `usage.{prompt_tokens, completion_tokens}`. The `Action` tag-typed enum is parsed in the **turn loop**, not the provider; providers return text.
764	
765	Cancellation: `tokio::select!` on `token.cancelled()` vs `client.post().send()` (`lib.rs:226-263`).
766	
767	### 10.4 CLI sub-agent adapters
768	
769	**`cli:claude-code` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_claude_code.rs:1-127`).** Invocation:
770	
771	```zsh
772	claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p "<prompt>"
773	```
774	
775	The `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag is non-negotiable (no human is in the loop). The subprocess runs **inside** the deadreckon sandbox profile, so Claude's bypass only disables its own permission gate; deadreckon's outer Seatbelt/bwrap still scopes the process. Stdout is captured to `request.output_path` (the turn's `claude.out`).
776	
777	**`cli:codex` (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_codex.rs:1-143`).** Invocation:
778	
779	```zsh
780	codex --ask-for-approval never exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox <mode> "<prompt>"
781	```
782	
783	`<mode>` (`cli_codex.rs:121-131`) is `workspace-write` when the outer sandbox is `None`/`SandboxBackend::None` (safer, codex limits itself to cwd), and `danger-full-access` when an outer sandbox is active (the outer sandbox is doing the isolating; codex needs full filesystem access inside).
784	
785	**Shared subprocess machinery (`cli_common.rs:22-120`).** Builds a `SandboxSpec` with explicit allowlists (`cli_common.rs:154-166`):
786	
787	- Write allowlist: `~/.codex` for codex, `~/.claude` for claude.
788	- Read allowlist: binary location + `~/.bun`, `~/.local`, `~/.npm-global`, `~/.opencode`.
789	- `allow_network: true` (CLI agents need outbound for their own API calls).
790	
791	**Spend (subscription).** Per `cli_claude_code.rs:100-110` and the equivalent in `cli_codex.rs`:
792	
793	```rust
794	SpendEstimate {
795	    cost_usd: 0.0,
796	    subscription: true,
797	    wall_time_seconds: Some(elapsed),
798	}
799	```

```text
1	# Multi-Run Coordination
2	
3	Lock ordering is scope first, run second.
4	
5	Rules:
6	
7	1. Compute the workspace scope from the git root or `DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT`.
8	2. Acquire the scope/task lock at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/locks/<scope>--<task>.lock`.
9	3. Only after the scope lock is held, mutate files under `runstate/<scope>/runs/<run-id>/`.
10	4. Never acquire locks in the reverse order.
11	5. Release is idempotent; stale lock reclaim uses heartbeat age plus PID liveness.
12	
13	Different scopes may run the same task key concurrently. A second run in the same scope/task is refused with the first run id and phase so the operator can attach, kill, or resume the owner.
14
```

```text
1	# Resume Semantics
2	
3	deadreckon resumes from durable runstate, not model memory.
4	
5	Ordering:
6	
7	1. Load `state.json`.
8	2. Read `traces.jsonl` line by line and keep only complete JSON entries.
9	3. Reconstruct tool-result history from complete `tool.*` trace entries when `history.json` is missing or `--from-turn` is supplied.
10	4. If `--from-turn N` is supplied, truncate history to turn `N`, set `state.turn = N`, and continue with turn `N + 1`.
11	5. Ignore any partial trailing trace entry. The next turn replays from the last complete tool boundary.
12	
13	This makes a kill between provider response and tool dispatch recoverable: the partial trace is treated as advisory residue, never as completed work.
14
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
122	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len());

124	    for ch in input.chars() {
125	        let next = if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
126	            last_dash = false;
127	            Some(ch.to_ascii_lowercase())
128	        } else if matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | ' ' | '.') {
129	            if last_dash {
130	                None
131	            } else {
132	                last_dash = true;
133	                Some('-')
134	            }
135	        } else {
136	            None
137	        };
138	        if let Some(ch) = next {
139	            out.push(ch);
140	        }
141	    }
142	    out.trim_matches('-').to_string()
143	}
144	
145	fn find_git_root(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
146	    let mut cursor = if start.is_file() {
147	        start.parent()?.to_path_buf()
148	    } else {
149	        start.to_path_buf()
150	    };
151	    loop {
152	        if cursor.join(".git").exists() {
153	            return Some(cursor);
154	        }
155	        if !cursor.pop() {
156	            return None;
157	        }
158	    }
159	}
160	
161	fn fnv1a32(input: &str) -> u32 {
162	    let mut hash = 0x811c_9dc5u32;
163	    for byte in input.as_bytes() {
164	        hash ^= u32::from(*byte);
165	        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
166	    }
167	    hash
168	}
```

```text
182	pub fn create_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, options: RunOptions) -> Result<PipelineState> {
183	    let scope = workspace_scope(&options.cwd)?;
184	    let task_key = task_key(&options.goal);
185	    let run_id = options
186	        .run_id
187	        .unwrap_or_else(|| Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string());
188	    let run_root = paths.run_root(&scope, &run_id);
189	    let codebase = options.codebase.unwrap_or_else(CodebaseRecord::fresh);
190	    let working_dir = working_dir_for_codebase(&run_root, &codebase);
191	    fs::create_dir_all(&working_dir).with_path(&working_dir)?;
192	    fs::create_dir_all(run_root.join("snapshots")).with_path(run_root.join("snapshots"))?;
193	    let gate_dir = run_root.join("gate");
194	    fs::create_dir_all(&gate_dir).with_path(&gate_dir)?;
195	    fs::write(gate_dir.join("nonce"), Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string())
196	        .with_path(gate_dir.join("nonce"))?;
197	
198	    // AS-BUILT §3: the binary owns deterministic paths while the skill stays a
199	    // markdown subprocess boundary under the source tree.
200	    let skill_path = PathBuf::from(SOURCE_ROOT)
201	        .join("skills")
202	        .join(&options.skill_name)
203	        .join("SKILL.md");
204	    let now = Utc::now();
205	    let mut state = PipelineState {
206	        version: STATE_VERSION,
207	        goal: options.goal,
208	        task_key,
209	        run_id,
210	        scope,
211	        status: RunStatus::Pending,
212	        current_phase_id: PhaseId(0),
213	        started_at: now,
214	        updated_at: now,
215	        cwd: options.cwd,
216	        run_root,
217	        working_dir,
218	        skill_name: options.skill_name,
219	        skill_path,
220	        sandbox: options.sandbox,
221	        provider: options.provider,
222	        max_spend_usd: options.max_spend_usd,
223	        max_wall_seconds: options.max_wall_seconds,
224	        total_spend_usd: 0.0,
225	        total_wall_seconds: 0.0,
226	        turn: 0,
227	        pause_reason: None,
228	        failure_reason: None,
229	        child_pids: Vec::new(),
230	        killed_at: None,
231	        promoted_library_dir: None,
232	        phases: default_phases(now),
233	    };
234	    state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(0), PhaseStatus::Planned)?;
235	    save_state(&state)?;
236	    write_codebase_record(&state.working_dir, &codebase)?;
237	    ensure_docs_started(&state)?;
238	    write_current_pointer(paths, &state)?;
```

```text
107	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
108	pub enum ResolvedMode {
109	    Worktree {
110	        source_path: PathBuf,
111	        git_root: PathBuf,
112	    },
113	    Copy {
114	        source_path: PathBuf,
115	    },
116	    InPlace {
117	        source_path: PathBuf,
118	    },
119	    Fresh,
120	}
121	
122	impl ResolvedMode {
123	    pub fn mode(&self) -> CodebaseMode {
124	        match self {
125	            Self::Worktree { .. } => CodebaseMode::Worktree,
126	            Self::Copy { .. } => CodebaseMode::Copy,
127	            Self::InPlace { .. } => CodebaseMode::InPlace,
128	            Self::Fresh => CodebaseMode::Fresh,
129	        }
130	    }
131	}
132	
133	pub fn resolve_mode(flags: &ModeFlags, cwd: &Path, tty: bool) -> Result<ResolvedMode> {
134	    if flags.fresh {
135	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Fresh);
136	    }
137	    if flags.in_place {
138	        if !flags.i_know_its_a_lot && !tty {
139	            return Err(user_error(
140	                "--in-place requires --i-know-its-a-lot or interactive confirm",
141	                "add --i-know-its-a-lot or run in a TTY",
142	            ));
143	        }
144	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::InPlace {
145	            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
146	        });
147	    }
148	    if let Some(source_path) = flags.from.as_ref() {
149	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Copy {
150	            source_path: canonical_or_self(source_path)?,
151	        });
152	    }
153	    if flags.worktree {
154	        let git_root = find_git_root(cwd)?.ok_or_else(|| {
155	            user_error(
156	                &format!("{} is not a git repo", cwd.display()),
157	                "git init or pass --from .",
158	            )
159	        })?;
160	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Worktree {
161	            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
162	            git_root,
163	        });
164	    }
165	    if let Some(git_root) = find_git_root(cwd)? {
166	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Worktree {
167	            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
168	            git_root,
169	        });
170	    }
171	    if tty {
172	        return Ok(ResolvedMode::Copy {
173	            source_path: canonical_or_self(cwd)?,
174	        });
175	    }
176	    Err(user_error(
177	        "non-interactive without a mode flag",
178	        "--fresh or --from . or git init",
179	    ))
180	}
181	
182	pub fn record_for_resolved_mode(mode: ResolvedMode) -> CodebaseRecord {
183	    let mut record = CodebaseRecord::fresh();
184	    match mode {
185	        ResolvedMode::Fresh => {}
186	        ResolvedMode::Copy { source_path } => {
187	            record.mode = CodebaseMode::Copy;
188	            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
189	        }
190	        ResolvedMode::InPlace { source_path } => {
191	            record.mode = CodebaseMode::InPlace;
192	            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
193	        }
194	        ResolvedMode::Worktree {
195	            source_path,
196	            git_root,
197	        } => {
198	            record.mode = CodebaseMode::Worktree;
199	            record.source_path = Some(source_path);
200	            record.source_git_root = Some(git_root);
201	        }
202	    }
203	    record
204	}
205	
206	pub fn prepare_worktree_record(
207	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
208	    options: WorktreeOptions,
209	) -> Result<CodebaseRecord> {
210	    let git_root = find_git_root(&options.source_path)?.ok_or_else(|| {
211	        user_error(
212	            &format!("{} is not a git repo", options.source_path.display()),
213	            "git init or pass --from .",
214	        )
215	    })?;
216	    let base_ref = options
217	        .base_ref
218	        .unwrap_or_else(|| current_branch(&git_root).unwrap_or_else(|_| "HEAD".to_string()));
219	    preflight_worktree(&git_root, &base_ref, options.allow_dirty)?;
220	    let branch_name = options.branch_name.unwrap_or_else(|| {
221	        format!(
222	            "dr/{}-{}",
223	            options.task_key.chars().take(32).collect::<String>(),
224	            options.run_id.chars().take(8).collect::<String>()
225	        )
226	    });
227	    if git_ref_exists(&git_root, &branch_name)? {
228	        return Err(user_error(
229	            &format!("branch {branch_name} already exists"),
230	            "pass --branch <other-name>",
231	        ));
232	    }
233	    let scope = workspace_scope(&git_root)?;
234	    let worktree_path = unique_worktree_path(paths, &scope, &options.run_id);
235	    let base_sha = git_stdout(&git_root, &["rev-parse", &base_ref])?;
236	    let mut record = CodebaseRecord::fresh();
237	    record.mode = CodebaseMode::Worktree;
238	    record.source_path = Some(canonical_or_self(&options.source_path)?);
239	    record.source_git_root = Some(git_root);
240	    record.branch_name = Some(branch_name);
241	    record.base_ref = Some(base_ref);
242	    record.base_sha = Some(base_sha);
243	    record.worktree_path = Some(worktree_path);
244	    record.dirty_files_seeded = options.allow_dirty;
245	    Ok(record)
246	}
247	
248	pub fn create_worktree(record: &CodebaseRecord) -> Result<()> {
249	    if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
250	        return Ok(());
251	    }
252	    let git_root = required_path(record.source_git_root.as_ref(), "source_git_root")?;
253	    let worktree_path = required_path(record.worktree_path.as_ref(), "worktree_path")?;
254	    let branch = required_string(record.branch_name.as_deref(), "branch_name")?;
255	    let base = required_string(record.base_ref.as_deref(), "base_ref")?;
256	    if let Some(parent) = worktree_path.parent() {
257	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
258	    }
259	    git_status(
260	        git_root,
261	        &[
262	            "worktree",
263	            "add",
264	            "-b",
265	            branch,
266	            path_str(worktree_path)?,
267	            base,
268	        ],
269	    )?;
270	    append_git_exclude(git_root, ".deadreckon/")?;
271	    if record.dirty_files_seeded {
272	        seed_dirty_files(git_root, worktree_path)?;
273	    }
274	    Ok(())
275	}
```

```text
## Team Collaboration Synthesis: Unmet Needs in deadreckon Goal+Rider Pairs

Based on a comprehensive read of all 14 goal+rider pairs across `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/`, I've extracted the unmet needs and pain points that reveal hidden team collaboration requirements. The product was designed as single-user, single-machine—but many of the deepest pains the goals articulate are actually team-shaped problems constrained by that boundary.

### Part 2: Recurring Themes

Grouping the "team-collab smell" items above into 3–6 recurring themes:

#### **Theme 1: Audit, Review, and Sign-Off Need a Separate Reviewer**
- **Self-contained runs**: The `dr-gate` acceptance spec and proof signing are designed to prevent the agent from marking itself done. But the signer is _implicit_ (the user, running the gate binary locally).
- **Review surface for teammates**: `apply` / `abandon` are one-way (user decides). No affordance for "teammate reviews my PR and approves."
- **Multi-step approval workflows** are explicitly V1 in the build rider (line 331 of build-rider). But the need is real: "I want my teammate to gate my run before it auto-applies."
- **Pairs affected**: codebase, orchestrate, audit-harden.
- **The natural team framing**: When the signer is local, it's "self-attestation prevention." When the signer is a teammate (or CI), it's "approval workflow." The harness has the vocab (gate, proof, signature) but no team boundary.

#### **Theme 2: Library is Built for Individual Discovery, Not Team Sharing**
- **Promoted runs land in scoped library**: `~/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/` is personal inventory by default. `library list|search|show` is scoped to the local machine.
- **Team memory is unshared**: "I want to find all image-processing tasks my teammates have done" requires either access to teammates' `~/.deadreckon/` directories (none) or a shared index (not built). The audit rider landed `library search <pattern>`, which is powerful—but single-user.
- **No access control**: Every run in my library is visible to me; no "team runs" vs. "personal runs"; no read-only share of a specific run's docs to reviewers.
- **Pairs affected**: usability, self-documenting, audit-harden, doc-depth.
- **The natural team framing**: When you land a high-quality run, you want to share the docs + code diff with the team. Not in scope: "export run to a shared wiki" (line 327 of build-rider: "Run handoff and sharing" is V1). But the docs are ready to share; the harness is not.

#### **Theme 3: Orchestration and Parallel Work Are Single-Machine Scoped**
- **Plan + fork + merge**: The orchestrate rider decomposes a goal into N sub-goals and spawns children on the local machine, in distinct scopes, with a multi-pane TUI. Merge resolves conflicts via prefer-child strategy.
- **The missing piece**: "My teammate takes sub-goal 1, I take sub-goal 2, we merge results." That's orchestrate on a team. Today, orchestrate is one person coordinating N agents on one machine (or in one worktree group).
- **Lock ordering is documented** (MULTI-RUN.md) to prevent cross-scope state bleed. But there's no cross-machine lock; two teammates can unknowingly race on the same codebase.
- **Conflict resolution** (prefer-child, default) only works when both writes happened in the same merge. Cross-machine: two teammates both edited the same file → no merge, just a git conflict in the main repo. Not in scope.
- **Pairs affected**: orchestrate, autonomous-chain, codebase.
- **The natural team framing**: Orchestrate decomposes a goal; a team distributes work. The harness has goal decomposition (plan); the missing layer is work distribution (CI, queue, scheduler). Build rider line 308: "Sub-agent forking with context isolation" and AS-BUILT §22 point to the gap.

#### **Theme 4: Heterogeneous Agents Need Unified Routing, Not Just Provider Abstraction**
- **Five agents on five branches** (REPORT.md need #2): Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, etc. Different UIs, different permissions models, different output shapes.
- **Import normalizes history**: `deadreckon import claude-code|codex|cursor` reads and normalizes into traces.jsonl + provenance.jsonl. Cross-tool state sharing is read-only (audit rider, §6).
- **Provider registry makes it pluggable**: New in provider-registry goal. A user can configure any provider and route by flag or default. But there's no "when in this repo, prefer Codex; when in that repo, prefer Claude Code" logic. Configuration is binary-local, not codebase-aware.
- **Team case**: "Our team uses Claude Code for code, Cursor for editing, Codex for research. How do I route tasks to the right agent?" The provider registry is extensible, but the router is policy-dumb.
- **Pairs affected**: build, primary-flow, provider-registry.
- **The natural team framing**: Heterogeneous agents arise when teams have mixed subscriptions or tooling. Single-user: "which provider do I use today?" Team: "which provider should this task use, given our team's constraints?" Out of scope in build rider: "Cost-aware provider routing" (line 312) and "Versioned team prompt libraries" (line 333).

#### **Theme 5: Workspaces and Scopes Are Designed for Solo Machine Isolation, Not Team Boundaries**
- **Scopes isolate runs**: `<scope>` is derived from git root or env var. Prevents lock collision on one machine. But "one machine" is the assumption.
- **Worktree as isolation primitive**: Codebase rider makes git worktrees the default. Isolation is perfect: one worktree = one agent, one set of edits, one branch. Multi-agent on one machine works. Multi-agent on multiple machines: each has their own worktree on their own machine; no merge strategy except "last one to apply wins."
- **No shared scope metadata**: A scope is just a string (hash of git root). No team identifier, no owner, no "this is [team-name]'s scope." Scopes are fungible per user.
- **Pairs affected**: codebase, orchestrate, robust.
- **The natural team framing**: When teammates work on the same codebase, they need a shared scope concept: "this is the team-frontend project." Then tooling (hooks, approval gates) can be team-scoped. Not in scope: "Cloud sync of histories" (build rider, line 330).

#### **Theme 6: Handoff is Unidirectional; Feedback from Teammates is Out of Scope**
- **Materialize and extend**: After completion, the user can `materialize` (copy library to user dest) and `extend` (re-run with new goal, seeded from parent). But a teammate cannot "pick up" the work if the original user is offline. Copies are local; no "my teammate picks up my run from the shared repo."
- **Export is V1**: "Run handoff and sharing" (build rider, line 327) is explicitly deferred. Export exists in the codebase rider (apply merges), but export to a tar.zst + push to remote is not built.
- **No approval workflow**: The user applies their own run. A teammate cannot review and approve on their behalf. Multi-step approvals are V1 (line 331).
- **Pairs affected**: usability, codebase, audit-harden.
- **The natural team framing**: Handoff works when the original user is the final decision-maker. In a team, handoff is "I'm done with this part; can you take it from here?" and later "Done; here's what changed." No team affordance for "my teammate reviewed my work and approved it."

### Part 4: Identity & Path Assumptions Baked In

Single-user/single-machine assumptions in invariants:

1. **User-local state**: `~/.deadreckon/` is assumed to be user-private. No multi-user guard on state read/write. Scopes isolate runs on one machine, but not users.
2. **Single `config.toml`**: One provider config per user (`/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`). No per-machine, per-team, or per-codebase override hierarchy (beyond codebase.json for mode metadata). Provider registry adds `~/.deadreckon/providers.d/`, which is user-local only.
3. **Worktree isolation**: Worktrees are per-machine (`~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<id>/`). Branch is per-git-root. Two machines with clones of the same repo will each create their own worktree + branch. No synchronization.
4. **Promoted library is machine-local**: `~/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/` is on the user's machine. No sync, no indexing, no cross-machine discovery.
5. **Lock is process-local with PID liveness probe**: Locks are acquired on the local machine via advisory locks (nix) + PID kill(pid, 0) liveness. Cross-machine locks would require a server (not in scope).
6. **Sandbox runs on the local machine**: sandbox-exec (macOS), bwrap (Linux), Docker (if opted in). No remote sandboxes (E2B, Modal, etc. are V1 candidates).
7. **Gates run on the local machine**: dr-gate is a binary invoked locally. Acceptance proof is local. No remote approval server.
8. **Skills are filesystem-loaded**: Skills (SKILL.md) are loaded from `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/`, `~/.deadreckon/skills/`, or per-codebase `<source>/skills/`. Shared skill libraries would need a registry or package manager (not in scope).
9. **Hooks are filesystem-loaded**: `~/.deadreckon/hooks/chain/{pre-step,post-step,on-promote,on-chain-end}` are shell scripts on the local machine. No distributed hook system.

---

### Part 5: Five Highest-Impact Unmet Team-Collab Needs

Synthesized from the pairs and themes above:

1. **Approval workflows and multi-step sign-off** (relates to: codebase, orchestrate, audit-harden, autonomous-chain)
   - **Need**: When a run completes, a teammate should be able to review the changes and approve (or request changes) before the code auto-applies to the team's main branch. Today, the user's local `apply` is the only gate.
   - **Why team framing is natural**: In a team, the person who ran the agent (e.g., "fix the off-by-one") is not the person who decides "is this safe to land?" That's a code-review step. The harness has acceptance gates (dr-gate) to prevent self-attestation, but the reviewer is always local and implicit (the user running deadreckon apply).

2. **Shared run history and library discovery across teammates** (relates to: self-documenting, audit-harden, doc-depth, orchestrate)
   - **Need**: A teammate should be able to search and read the docs from prior runs (mine, theirs, anyone's on the team) without manual copy-paste or cross-machine access. `library list|search|show` is powerful but single-user and single-machine.
   - **Why team framing is natural**: Run docs are generated for "future-you" or "someone reading this later." In a team, "later" often means "a teammate." High-quality run narratives (stoa-shaped) are team assets, not personal notes. The harness produces them; team sharing is a distribution problem.

3. **Work distribution and task queuing for parallel team efforts** (relates to: orchestrate, autonomous-chain, robust)
   - **Need**: When a goal is decomposed (`plan`, `fork`), the sub-tasks should be assignable to teammates' machines, with a coordinator tracking progress and auto-merging results. Today, `fork` spawns all children on one machine.
   - **Why team framing is natural**: Orchestrate decomposes a goal into sub-goals (a team problem). The harness implements goal decomposition and single-machine orchestration (fork/merge/kill). Multi-machine: "sub-goal 1 runs on Alice's machine, sub-goal 2 on Bob's" requires a queue or work-distribution layer. That's V1 (line 308 of build-rider: "Sub-agent forking with context isolation" + AS-BUILT §22 "scheduler/queue is missing").

4. **Team-scoped credentials, hooks, and routing policies** (relates to: provider-registry, build, autonomous-chain)
   - **Need**: A team wants to "use Claude Code by default for coding, Codex for research; all machines use the team's OpenAI key; hooks enforce style checks before auto-apply." Today, each user/machine has a local config, provider routing is policy-dumb, and hooks are local scripts.
   - **Why team framing is natural**: When a team adopts deadreckon, they want to codify team policies (which provider, which gate, which approval workflow) in one place (a team repo, a config service, a shared hook registry). Single-user: "I use Claude Code today, OpenAI tomorrow; I run lint when I feel like it." Team: "We all use the same provider; we all run lint before apply." Team config is deferred.

5. **Handoff and resumption across teammates and machines** (relates to: usability, codebase, primary-flow, distribute)
   - **Need**: When a run is unfinished or needs review, a teammate should be able to resume it (e.g., `resume <run-id>` on their machine after the original user goes offline), or at least import the work into a new run seeded with prior history. Today, resume is local; `extend` works but requires the original run to be completed and locally accessible.
   - **Why team framing is natural**: In a team, "my machine crashed" becomes "my teammate's machine crashed; can someone else continue?" Resumption across machines requires either (a) shared state (cloud sync, deferred), (b) hand-off via export/import (build rider line 327, V1), or (c) attach-to-remote (build rider TUI expansions). The harness has the primitives (history.json, state.json, traces.jsonl); distribution is the gap.

---

## Summary

deadreckon's 14 goal+rider pairs reveal a single consistent gap: **the harness is architected for one user, one machine, but every major goal touches multi-user or multi-machine pain in disguise.**

The clearest signals:
- **Orchestration, codebase, and usability pairs** all name single-machine constraints that become team problems.
- **Self-documenting and doc-depth pairs** produce team-quality docs but with no team-sharing surface.
- **Build rider explicitly defers** seven team-collab features (handoff, approval workflows, team libraries, etc.) as V1/V2 candidates.
- **Audit rider names** "multi-human handoff" and "queue orchestration" as V1.

The five highest-impact unmet needs form a coherent story: **approval workflows + shared discovery + work distribution + team policies + cross-machine resumption.** Together, they unlock the transition from "deadreckon for a solo developer" to "deadreckon for a heterogeneous team running 5 different CLI agents on 5 different machines, with shared code, shared decisions, and team governance."

The harness is 85% of the way there. The missing 15% is team boundaries, not harness internals.
```

```text
12	**Core idea.** A *plan* = one goal decomposed into N sub-goals. Each becomes a *child run* under the normal turn loop, in its own sub-scope, with its own working dir, lock, sandbox, provider, gate. A *coordinator* owns the plan, supervises children, exposes a multi-pane attach view, and on completion atomically merges children's `library/` outputs into a merge working dir that goes through the gate again before promotion. A child is a normal `deadreckon run` plus a `parent_plan_id` in its `.deadreckon/parent.json`.

15	
16	- `plan <goal>` — provider decomposes into N sub-goals; writes `plan.json`.
17	- `fork <plan-id>` — spawns one child per sub-goal; prints attach/merge/kill hints.
18	- `attach <plan-id>` — multi-pane TUI; Enter drills, Esc returns, Ctrl-D detaches.
19	- `merge <plan-id>` — composes children's `library/`, gates the merged result, promotes.
20	- `kill <plan-id>` — cascades SIGTERM → SIGKILL(2s) to every child + coordinator.
21	- `history grep <pattern>` — over `library/**/traces.jsonl`; `--plan` scopes to one plan.
22	- `show <id> --why-failed` — RCA over failure-adjacent traces. Works for runs and plans.
```

1339	## 21. Key Design Decisions
1340	
1341	1. **No new `PipelineState` fields without a strong reason.** Parent lineage, materialization status, and other run-level metadata live in files inside the working tree (e.g., `.deadreckon/parent.json`), not on the state struct. This keeps `state.json` migration-safe.
1342	
1343	2. **Two-layer split is non-negotiable.** Skills (Markdown) own judgment; the binary owns invariants. A skill cannot bypass the gate; a gate cannot read prompts.
1344	
1345	3. **Anti-self-attestation via a nonce only `dr-gate` reads.** The agent can produce any output it wants; it cannot produce a valid `AcceptanceMarker.signature` because it never sees `gate/nonce`.
1346	
1347	4. **Atomic promotion before completion.** `Completed` is set only after the library swap succeeds. If promotion fails, the run fails. This means a `Completed` status always implies a durable artifact in `library/`.
1348	
1349	5. **Platform-native sandboxing.** No Docker daemon dependency. Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux. Docker is opt-in. The "running on host machine feels like a bad idea" pain point is solved without forcing Docker.
1350	
1351	6. **BYOK extends to subscriptions.** `cli:claude-code` and `cli:codex` are first-class providers, not afterthoughts. Most users will run deadreckon via subscription, not API keys.
1352	
1353	7. **Phase numbering with gaps (0, 10, 20, …).** Future phases can be inserted (e.g., a phase 15 for plan refinement) without rewriting durable state.
1354	
1355	8. **Append-only telemetry.** `spend.jsonl`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, `events.jsonl` are immutable audit trails. The TUI and `show` command read them; nothing rewrites them.
1356	
1357	9. **The smoke provider is a real provider.** `--smoke` selects `ScriptedSmokeProvider`, which goes through the same `ProviderRouter::complete` path. There is no separate "smoke turn loop" — the loop is always the loop.
1358	
1359	10. **PID-aware locks with stale reclaim.** A crashed deadreckon process can be detected (its lock holder PID is dead via `kill(pid, 0)`); the next run reclaims the lock. No external lock daemon.
1360
