# deadreckon GitHub-Coupled Team Sync: Adoption Likelihood Assessment

## 1. Target user characterization

The deadreckon docs describe the user with unusual specificity, and that user is *not* a 5-person mixed-tooling team. Pulling the receipts:

- **"You bring the agent CLI you already trust"** — the README opens by anchoring on Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor CLI as upstream agents (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md:9-11`). The user is already a heavy CLI user with a chosen agent. Not someone GitHub-issue-driven.
- **"You can leave a long run going and trust the result"** (`README.md:32`) — the value prop is *single-operator unattended autonomy*, not coordination.
- **"Walk away, attach later from any terminal"** (`README.md:17`) — the durability story serves *one person's* multi-device life (laptop closes, phone tethers in, attach from desktop later), not *multiple people* watching the same run.
- **Local-first runtime.** The DESIGN.md is explicit: *"The alpha implementation is intentionally local-first. Runtime state defaults to `~/.deadreckon/`"* (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/DESIGN.md:7`). Every artifact path the proposed feature wants to publish lives under `~/.deadreckon/`, by deliberate choice.
- **BYOK posture.** Provider routing in §10 of AS-BUILT covers Anthropic / OpenAI / OpenAI-compatible HTTP plus `cli:claude-code` / `cli:codex` subscription wrappers. These users hold their own keys / subscriptions; they are not in a procurement-managed team license model.
- **V1 list is one item: `deadreckon fork`** (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`). Cloud sync of histories is *explicitly* listed under "not yet built" in AS-BUILT §22 (`docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1421`). The author has already classified team-sync as out of scope for the current product surface.
- **Sandbox + watchdog discipline.** The `dr-gate` watchdog, signed acceptance markers, and per-turn snapshots are anti-self-attestation features. The user fears being lied to by their *own* agent — a single-operator trust problem, not a Slack-coordination problem.

**Honest read of the target user:** a senior individual contributor or small-OSS-maintainer profile, comfortable with Rust toolchain and `cargo`, already running one specific agent CLI under a paid subscription, who lets long runs go overnight and wants forensic-grade recovery if anything goes wrong. The "5-person team where Alice/Bob/Carol use different agents" persona does not appear anywhere in the docs as a current user. It is a *roadmap user*, and the roadmap (V1-CANDIDATES.md) doesn't even have it.

This matters because the proposed feature reverses the polarity of *every* product decision deadreckon has made so far: local → cloud, single-operator → team, "agent can't lie" → "team can verify the artifact", `~/.deadreckon/` private → `git notes` public. None of that is wrong, but it's a *new product*, not a feature increment.

## 2. Adoption precedents

**`gh` CLI itself.** Stack Overflow 2025 places GitHub at 81% of developers as their primary code collab tool [Stack Overflow 2025](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/). 35% of new repos in 2023 were created via `gh` ([GitHub gh CLI manual](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_login)). That's the high-water mark for a GitHub-native CLI. Note: 35% of *repo creation* is not 35% of *all developers having `gh auth login` configured for their daily org*. The org-scoped authorization step (SAML SSO) is its own gate — see friction inventory below.

**Aider.** 39k stars, ~4M installs ([Aider repo](https://github.com/Aider-AI/aider)). Aider has *no* PR-publishing flow. It has a `--commit` flag and stops there. Despite being the most-adopted open-source terminal coding agent, it deliberately does *not* couple itself to GitHub-the-platform. Lesson: the most successful CLI in deadreckon's neighborhood adopted the *opposite* posture from the proposed feature.

**Copilot Workspace.** Sunset May 30, 2025 ([Copilot Workspace 2025 → 2026 transition](https://www.javacodegeeks.com/2026/02/github-copilot-workspace-the-agentic-era.html)). The "agent run as draft PR" UX failed in the most well-funded, most GitHub-native, most-distribution-advantaged setting possible. GitHub kept the *capability* (Coding Agent + Mission Control) but explicitly retreated from "every agent run is a PR." This is the single most damning precedent for the proposed design — the company that *owns* draft PRs tried "agent run = draft PR" and walked it back.

**`pre-commit`.** Universal because it sits at *the user's own* git seam, requires zero remote auth, and produces no PRs. Adoption story: gradient-of-engagement (run locally → commit hook → CI). Not a precedent for the proposed design; it's a precedent for a *much smaller* version of it.

**`act` (nektos).** ~70k stars, succeeds because it makes the *existing* GitHub Actions abstraction runnable locally ([nektos/act](https://github.com/nektos/act)). It rides existing primitives instead of introducing new ones. Lesson: extend, don't create.

**Sapling vs Graphite.** Sapling (Meta-quality, very polished) is niche-adopted; Graphite (lighter, web UI hooks) is broader. The lesson is grim for the proposed design: even *opinionated stacked-PR UX with a slick web product behind it* hasn't displaced raw `git` in most teams. A "git notes index of agent runs" has even less polish leverage.

**Renovate / Dependabot bot-PR fatigue.** Documented cases of 200 PRs/week, "alert fatigue," PRs closed without review ([Renovate docs noise reduction](https://docs.renovatebot.com/noise-reduction/), [Dependabot fatigue thread](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/discussions/42473)). Auto-publishing bot-created draft PRs is widely considered a *negative* signal in 2026, not a positive one. Maintainers have learned to filter bot PRs. A `deadreckon` PR will look like another bot PR unless and until reviewers learn to trust the author.

**`changesets`.** Adopted because it sits between dev and CI as a *human-authored* opt-in artifact (`.changeset/*.md`). Not auto-published. Closer precedent for "commit the artifact, let humans decide what to do with it."

**Git notes.** "Git's coolest, most unloved feature" ([Tyler Cipriani](https://tylercipriani.com/blog/2022/11/19/git-notes-gits-coolest-most-unloved-feature/)). GitHub *removed* git-notes display from its UI years ago. Not auto-fetched, not in any tool's default UX. As a *team registry*, git notes will be invisible. Anything that depends on `refs/notes/dr-runs` for human discovery is dead on arrival in 2026.

**Check Runs API — the architectural gotcha.** This is the single biggest finding of this research. *Write* access to Check Runs is **GitHub-Apps-only**; OAuth tokens and PATs cannot create check runs ([GitHub docs: Using the REST API to interact with checks](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/guides/using-the-rest-api-to-interact-with-checks)). The proposed `gh auth token` inheritance plan **cannot post `dr-gate` results as Check Runs**. To do that, deadreckon would need to ship a GitHub App, install it in the user's repo (and any org's repos), and route through it. That's a fundamentally different distribution and trust ask than `gh auth token`.

## 3. Friction inventory

Walking the first-time flow as a likely deadreckon user:

1. **First-run prompt: "publish this run as a draft PR?"** A user who chose deadreckon for "isolated worktree, your checkout never touched" (README) just got asked to publish to a remote. The cognitive whiplash is severe. The whole product narrative is *hermetic*. The first auto-publish offer reads as "we changed our minds about hermetic." Best-case response: "no, what does that even mean?" Worst-case: uninstall.

2. **`gh auth token` inheritance — works for some, breaks for many.** SAML SSO orgs require a separate per-PAT authorization step ([GitHub Enterprise docs](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/authentication/authenticating-with-single-sign-on/authorizing-a-personal-access-token-for-use-with-single-sign-on)). Many enterprises forbid classic PATs entirely. `gh auth token` returns a token that's valid for *some* of the user's orgs, sometimes silently. This produces "works in my personal repo, mysteriously fails for the work repo" — the worst possible failure mode for a try-it-out feature.

3. **Check Runs requires a GitHub App.** Cannot be done with `gh auth token`. Either drop Check Runs from the design, or commit to shipping and maintaining a GitHub App with all the marketplace, install-flow, and org-admin-approval consequences. There is no middle ground.

4. **Auto-creating draft PRs joins the bot-PR queue.** Renovate/Dependabot fatigue is real and well-documented. Reviewers in 2026 have a learned reflex to triage-by-author and filter bot PRs. A deadreckon-authored draft PR with 8MB of `provenance.jsonl` baked into the squash commit competes for the *same eyeball budget* as Dependabot, and loses, because dependency updates have established review heuristics and run artifacts don't.

5. **Solo OSS maintainer vs employee crossing many orgs — opposite auth shapes.** Solo: one `gh auth login`, things mostly work. Multi-org employee: each org has different SAML/PAT/App policies. The "one auth strategy" mental model the design implies (`gh` → keyring → env var) doesn't actually exist as one model. It's three layered fallbacks that each fail differently per org.

6. **`refs/notes/dr-runs` is invisible.** Even if it works, no team will discover it. GitHub's UI doesn't show it. `git fetch` doesn't pull it by default. A "team registry" that requires every team member to add `+refs/notes/dr-runs:refs/notes/dr-runs` to their fetch refspec is not a team registry. It's a private telemetry channel.

7. **Squash-commit-with-artifacts is a long-term repo-bloat conversation.** Committing `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `manifest.json`, `provenance.jsonl`, and failed-attempts into the squash commit means every developer who clones the repo carries *every agent's full run trail forever*. JSONL files compress poorly across deltas. Three engineers running 5 agent runs/day for a year = ~5,500 commits each with multi-MB JSONL appendages. Maintainers will reject this in code review the first time they see the diff size.

## 4. One-sentence adoption thesis

Honest version: **"This feature, as scoped, will not be adopted, because it requires a GitHub App for the Check Runs piece (which is a different product), it routes around the user's existing reflex (`gh pr create` already exists), and it commits binary-ish run artifacts into squash commits where reviewers have learned to filter exactly that kind of bot-authored noise."**

Generous version: **"This feature could be adopted *because* deadreckon already produces a uniquely high-quality `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` that nothing else in the agent CLI ecosystem produces, *only if* publication is opt-in, ships zero infrastructure (no GitHub App, no git notes), and treats the PR as a *handoff target* rather than an *automatic event*."**

The aspirational version of the original framing — "Alice/Bob/Carol on three different agents converge on one PR thread" — is not defensible from any data I found. It's a designer's dream user, not a documented one. Mark that thesis explicitly aspirational.

## 5. Low-friction fallback paths, ordered by adoption likelihood

**(a) `deadreckon pr` — manual subcommand, zero auto.** Generates a Markdown PR description from `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` + `RUN-DECISIONS.md` and either prints to stdout (pipe to `gh pr create --body-file -`) or, if `gh` is on PATH and authenticated, shells out to `gh pr create --draft --body-file …`. No artifact commits. No Check Runs. No git notes. The user opted in by typing `deadreckon pr`. Likely adoption: high among current users, because it surfaces an artifact they already value, costs them nothing if unused, and uses a verb they already type (`gh pr create`). This is a Phase-0 win.

**(b) `deadreckon apply --commit-narrative`.** Optional flag on the existing `apply` command: include `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` (only — not provenance/manifest) at `.deadreckon/last-run.md` in the squash commit. Single small file, overwritten each apply, opt-in via flag. Likely adoption: moderate. Reviewers read it, like it, ask for it.

**(c) `deadreckon publish` (file artifact, not PR).** Writes `.deadreckon/runs/<id>/` into the *worktree* before apply, and lets `apply` carry whatever the user wants. No PR, no Checks, no notes. Teams can adopt at their own pace via their existing `apply` flow. Likely adoption: moderate, but only by users who already work in teams.

**(d) Optional sidecar GitHub App.** A separately-distributed `deadreckon-checks` GitHub App that *only* posts Check Runs, installable from a marketplace listing. Decoupled from the CLI. Users who want it install it; everyone else ignores it. Likely adoption: low at first, possibly meaningful in 12+ months *if and only if* (a) and (b) drove organic team usage that creates demand. Building this before that demand exists is premature.

**(e) The full proposed design — auto-publish + Check Runs + git notes + artifact commits.** Likely adoption: very low, for the structural reasons above. Recommend deferring indefinitely.

## 6. Verdict

**GitHub-coupled team sync is not the right wedge for deadreckon at this phase.** The argument:

- The current product is **honest, narrow, and well-defined** (single-operator unattended autonomy with watchdog-enforced done). Every doc reinforces that. The proposed feature serves a different user.
- The single most-relevant precedent — Copilot Workspace's "agent run = draft PR" — was **sunset by GitHub itself** after a year of full corporate backing.
- The technical centerpiece (Check Runs via inherited token) **is not buildable as designed**. Check Runs requires a GitHub App, which is a different distribution model.
- The discoverability layer (git notes) **doesn't exist in any UI** that 2026 developers actually use.
- The PR-publishing default lands in a context where reviewers have **already learned to filter bot PRs**.

**What would have to be true for it to become the right wedge later:**
1. Evidence (telemetry, not vibes) that current deadreckon users are *manually* opening PRs from runs and pasting `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` content. If that signal exists, (a) above is the right next step. If it doesn't exist, none of this design serves a real user.
2. A second tier of user adopting the tool: a small team using it together. There's no evidence of that user today.
3. Willingness to ship and operate a GitHub App (security review, marketplace listing, install/uninstall flows, secret rotation). That's a real engineering line item, not a CLI feature.

**Yes-but-smaller version:** ship `deadreckon pr` (option (a)) as a *single-verb* feature — it's small, opt-in, costs nothing, and lets the next 6 months of usage data tell you whether team-coordination demand is real or aspirational. If `deadreckon pr` invocations grow, and especially if you see the same repo accumulate PRs from multiple users, *then* expand. If it stays flat, the V1 feature was always "explicit sub-agent forking" (per `V1-CANDIDATES.md`) and that's the honest next step. The current V1 list is right; don't displace it for a feature whose target user the docs don't yet describe.

The proposed framing — "team-collab pain disguised as single-user pain, the wedge is run artifact in git" — has an attractive ring, but the data I can find says the disguise is the message itself. If users haven't asked for team coordination, the pain isn't disguised; it's just not there yet.

# Stress-Test Report: deadreckon Team-Sync Design

## Claim 1: `octocrab` is the right Rust GitHub client

**Verdict: Confirmed (with caveats)**

**Evidence:**
- Active and current. Latest release is **v0.50.0 (May 5, 2026)** with releases roughly monthly across v0.49.x in March/April 2026. Stars ~1.4k, 341 forks. ([octocrab on GitHub](https://github.com/XAMPPRocky/octocrab), [releases](https://github.com/XAMPPRocky/octocrab/releases))
- Coverage: dedicated handlers for `checks`, `pulls` (incl. drafts), `commits`, releases, and GraphQL. ([octocrab docs](https://docs.rs/octocrab)).
- Auth: PAT (`personal_token`), GitHub App via `OctocrabBuilder::app` with `create_jwt` and per-installation token acquisition (cached and auto-refreshed), plus OAuth token exchange added in v0.50. ([`octocrab::auth`](https://docs.rs/octocrab/latest/octocrab/auth/index.html))
- Tokio-native (async-trait, hyper). ETag support exists via typed `Etagged<T>` and `.etag()` builder methods (efficient polling).
- Rate-limit handling is **partial**: there's a `ratelimit` handler module and v0.49.7 added "rate limit handling for retries", but the README explicitly warns about pagination: *"There's no rate limiting so be careful."* You must implement client-side throttling for bulk write loops.
- Configurable `base_uri` for GitHub Enterprise.
- Breaking changes are infrequent — a notable one in v0.50.0 (removed `either` dep), otherwise additive across v0.49.x.

**Alternatives:** `hubcaps` is dead (last release ~2021); `github-rs` likewise stale; `gh` Go SDK is not Rust. Hand-rolled `reqwest` is viable for a small surface (we likely touch only ~10 endpoints) but loses GitHub App JWT logic, retry hooks, and ETag types. Octocrab is the right choice.

**Implication:** Use octocrab. Implement our own simple budget for write-loop endpoints (PR body, notes-related calls). Don't lean on the built-in retry handler for primary loop pacing.

---

## Claim 2: `gh auth token` inheritance is a viable auth path

**Verdict: Confirmed**

**Evidence:**
- `gh auth token` prints the token to stdout and is documented as non-interactive — no TTY required. ([gh auth token](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_token))
- Multi-account: since gh v2.40, `gh` supports multiple accounts per host. By default `gh auth token` returns the *active* account's token; `--user <login>` and `--hostname <host>` disambiguate. ([cli/cli multiple-accounts.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cli/cli/trunk/docs/multiple-accounts.md))
- Cross-platform: works on macOS, Linux, Windows. The credential **storage** behind it varies (Keychain / libsecret / Windows Credential Manager / encrypted file fallback), but `gh auth token` abstracts that.
- Default scopes from `gh auth login --web`: `repo`, `read:org`, `gist`, `workflow`. Sufficient for branch push, PR create/update, commit comments, statuses. **Not** sufficient for Check Runs — see Claim 4.
- Failure modes: SSO-not-authorized returns a token that 401/403s on org repos; expired tokens are detectable via `/user` ping; fine-grained PATs honor only declared permissions.

**Implication:** Viable. The CLI should call `gh auth token` lazily, cache for the session, and on 401/403 print "your `gh` token may need `gh auth refresh` or SSO re-authorization."

---

## Claim 3: `keyring` (open-source-cooperative/keyring-rs) is the right Rust keyring

**Verdict: Partially confirmed**

**Evidence:**
- The crate moved from hwchen to **open-source-cooperative**, now maintained by Dan Brotsky. The original `keyring` crate is now a thin "sample code" facade; the real work is in `keyring-core` plus per-platform store crates. ([keyring-rs](https://github.com/open-source-cooperative/keyring-rs), [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/keyring))
- Linux is the painful platform: depends on `secret-service` (zbus pure-Rust async) or `dbus-secret-service` (libdbus C binding). Either way it requires a running Secret Service daemon (gnome-keyring, KWallet). On headless Linux/CI, this fails — the maintainers explicitly link to a workaround that starts a Gnome keyring unlocked with a known password. ([keyring docs Linux note](https://docs.rs/keyring/latest/keyring/secret_service/index.html))
- Dependency weight on Linux (zbus 4 + crypto features) is non-trivial but acceptable.
- No conflict with `gh`'s own keychain entries — different service names; they coexist, though it means a user could have two stored tokens (one per tool).

**Alternatives:** `secret-service` directly (Linux-only, more code), or simply *don't* persist a token of our own and always defer to `gh auth token`. The latter is the cleanest fallback for headless boxes.

**Implication:** Make `keyring` **optional**, behind a feature flag. On headless Linux, gracefully degrade to "env var > `gh auth token`" with no keyring write attempt. Don't fail to start because dbus is absent.

---

## Claim 4: GitHub Check Runs work for our use case

**Verdict: BROKEN for the primary OSS path**

**Evidence (this is the killer finding):**
- GitHub's REST docs are explicit: *"OAuth apps and personal access tokens (classic) cannot use this endpoint"* on update. Create likewise restricts write access to GitHub Apps. ([REST API for check runs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs))
- Fine-grained PATs cannot even *select* a Checks permission in the UI. GitHub support has confirmed: *"It isn't possible to assign Checks permissions to a Fine-grained PAT — only GitHub Apps can access this API."* ([community discussion #129512](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/129512))
- One community comment claims classic PATs work for the Checks API, but GitHub's own REST docs contradict this for the write endpoints. Even if it works today via `repo` scope, it's an undocumented edge that GitHub is actively deprecating.
- UI: GitHub App–owned check runs render with the App's avatar in the Checks tab. PAT-owned ones (where they work at all) appear as user activity, not first-class checks.

**Alternative — Commit Statuses API:** [`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/statuses/{sha}`](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/statuses) accepts a classic PAT with `repo:status` (or `repo`), and a fine-grained PAT with the **Commit statuses: write** permission. Renders as the older grey/yellow/green dot in the PR UI, with a `context`, `description`, and `target_url`. Less rich (no markdown body, no annotations) but PAT-friendly and works today.

**Implication — the design must change:**
- Drop Check Runs from the v1 OSS path. Use **Commit Statuses** with a stable `context` like `deadreckon/<run-id>` and a description like "turn 14/30 — running". Link `target_url` to the `.deadreckon/runs/<id>/INDEX.md` blob URL.
- Reserve Check Runs as an *optional* enhancement when the user installs an actual deadreckon GitHub App on their org (treat as the "premium" surfacing path, not the default).

---

## Claim 5: Git notes (`refs/notes/dr-runs`) are a viable team index

**Verdict: Broken**

**Evidence:**
- GitHub stopped rendering notes in its UI in 2014 and has not reinstated. Notes are invisible to anyone using the web UI. ([Git Notes: git's coolest, most unloved feature](https://tylercipriani.com/blog/2022/11/19/git-notes-gits-coolest-most-unloved-feature/))
- Adoption is genuinely thin. Most Git GUIs (GitHub Desktop, GitKraken, VS Code Git panel) don't surface notes. The intuition is correct.
- `refs/notes/*` is **not in the default fetch refspec** — every teammate must manually configure `fetch = +refs/notes/*:refs/notes/*` or invoke `git fetch origin "refs/notes/*:refs/notes/*"` explicitly. ([git-notes docs](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-notes))
- Concurrent writes: documented race in semantic-release CI shows `! [rejected] refs/notes/... (fetch first)` when two processes push notes to the same ref. `git notes merge` works *but* defaults to **manual** strategy (drops a `.git/NOTES_MERGE_WORKTREE` and waits for human intervention). Auto strategies (`union`, `cat_sort_uniq`, `theirs`, `ours`) exist but must be configured explicitly. ([git-notes merge strategies](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-notes))
- Even `union` only concatenates — for structured per-commit JSON, you'd need a custom merge driver.

**Alternative — `.deadreckon/team-index.jsonl`:** A normal tracked file, append-only JSONL, one line per turn or run-state change. Rebase/merge with a simple union driver (or just sort+uniq via .gitattributes). Pros: visible in PR diffs, searchable in GitHub UI, no extra fetch ritual, works on every host. Cons: shows up in PR diffs (noisy unless gitignored on dev branches).

**Implication — the design must change:**
- Drop `refs/notes/dr-runs` as the team index. Use a committed `.deadreckon/index/<run-id>.json` (or single `.deadreckon/team-index.jsonl`) with a documented `union` merge driver. Notes can remain a "power user" optional sync, but not the primary cross-team surface.

---

## Claim 6: GitHub API rate limits are manageable for per-turn PR body updates

**Verdict: Partially confirmed — secondary limits are the real risk**

**Evidence:**
- Primary: 5,000 req/hr authenticated user; 15,000/hr for GitHub Apps on Enterprise. ([rate limits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api))
- **Secondary content-creation limits**: *"no more than 80 content-generating requests per minute and no more than 500 content-generating requests per hour"*. PR body updates are content-generating. ([rate limits](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/rate-limits-for-the-rest-api))
- A 200-turn run that updates the PR body once per turn is comfortably under 500/hr **only if** turns are slower than ~7 seconds on average. Bursts of fast turns will trigger 429 with a `Retry-After`.
- Octocrab supports ETags via `Etagged<T>`, useful for read polling but not for write deduplication.
- Renovate and Dependabot batch comment/PR updates rather than streaming. They explicitly debounce.

**Implication:**
- Don't update the PR body per turn. Coalesce: write turn-level state to `.deadreckon/runs/<id>/turn-N.json` (cheap git operation), and only PATCH the PR body on (a) phase change, (b) every Nth turn, or (c) a 30-second debounce — whichever comes first. Honor `Retry-After` on 429.
- For the "live" surface, prefer commit statuses (also content-generating, but smaller payloads and arguably more idiomatic for "current state").

---

## Claim 7: Draft PRs can be created on push without prior PR existence

**Verdict: Partially confirmed**

**Evidence:**
- `gh pr create --draft` (and `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls` with `draft: true`) requires **at least one commit** between the head and base. Empty branches produce `No commits between main and <branch>`. ([cli/cli #9112](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9112), [#2691](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/2691))
- One commit is sufficient. The PR can be created the moment the first commit is pushed.
- The PAT user must have either push access to the upstream or be pushing to a fork; cross-repo PRs work, but the head must reference `fork-owner:branch`.
- Base branch auto-detection: gh uses the repo's default branch unless `--base` is given.

**Implication:**
- The design's "push branch then open draft PR" works as long as the first turn produces at least an empty commit (`git commit --allow-empty -m "deadreckon: run started"` is the safe primitive). Document this explicitly in the run-start sequence.

---

## Claim 8: GitHub repo permissions are sufficient ACL

**Verdict: Partially confirmed**

**Evidence:**
- A `repo`-scoped PAT inherits the user's full permissions, including any branch-protection bypass roles assigned to that user.
- Branch protection by default protects only the explicit branches/patterns configured (typically `main`, `release/*`). The `dr/*` namespace is exempt unless the org admin explicitly added it. Wildcard rules use `fnmatch` and don't cross `/`. ([branch protection rules](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/managing-a-branch-protection-rule))
- Force-push to `dr/*` works by default. A locked-down org might add a `*` or `**/*` wildcard — handle the failure gracefully.
- Forks: if the contributor has no push to upstream, the standard fork-and-PR flow works, but our CLI must detect "no push access" and offer to push to `origin` (assumed to be the user's fork) and open the PR `head: <user>:dr/<id>`. ([about forks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/working-with-forks/about-permissions-and-visibility-of-forks))

**Implication:**
- Probe push access at startup (cheap `gh api repos/o/r --jq .permissions.push`). On failure, switch to fork mode automatically: ensure a fork exists (`gh repo fork --remote`), push to the fork, open PR upstream.
- Document that `dr/*` should not be added to branch-protection wildcards.

---

## Claim 9: `keyring` + `gh auth token` + env-var three-tier auth is the right pattern

**Verdict: Partially confirmed — order should change**

**Evidence:**
- Common patterns in Rust GitHub-adjacent CLIs (cargo-binstall, cargo-dist) generally use: env var (`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GH_TOKEN`) first, then `gh` if available, with no native keyring.
- In Codespaces, `GITHUB_TOKEN` is auto-injected with restricted scope. There's a known issue where gh prefers `GITHUB_TOKEN` over its own stored token in Codespaces. ([cli/cli #6238](https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/6238))
- Order: gh's own precedence is `GH_TOKEN > GITHUB_TOKEN > stored credentials`. Mirroring this is least surprising.

**Implication — the design should change:**
- Order: `GH_TOKEN` > `GITHUB_TOKEN` > keyring > `gh auth token` > prompt. (gh-token last because gh itself may have been logged out, and keyring lets us persist a token across machines that don't have gh.)
- In Codespaces, the auto-injected `GITHUB_TOKEN` is restricted to the current repo and may lack PR write — detect Codespaces (`CODESPACES=true`) and warn if scopes are insufficient.
- Make keyring optional (Claim 3).

---

## Claim 10: Solo users see zero behavior change

**Verdict: Confirmed**

**Evidence:**
- `git remote -v` reliably exposes the URL; parsing for `github.com` (or `*.ghe.com` / configured Enterprise host) is straightforward via regex on both SSH (`git@github.com:o/r.git`) and HTTPS (`https://github.com/o/r(.git)?`).
- octocrab's `base_uri` makes self-hosted GHES first-class.
- Detection cascade: no remote → skip. Remote not GitHub → skip. GitHub remote, no token available → log a one-line "team-sync disabled (no auth)" and continue solo.

**Implication:**
- Hard-gate every team-sync code path on `is_github_repo() && has_token()`. Never call into octocrab at startup unconditionally. Solo mode must produce zero network traffic.

---

# The design must change in these 7 ways

1. **Replace Check Runs with Commit Statuses** as the v1 PR-UI surface (Claim 4). Reserve Check Runs as a future GitHub App tier.
2. **Replace `refs/notes/dr-runs` with a committed JSONL/JSON team index** under `.deadreckon/` (Claim 5). Drop notes from the v1 design entirely or reframe as opt-in extra.
3. **Debounce/coalesce PR body updates** to stay under the 500/hr secondary content-creation limit; honor `Retry-After` (Claim 6).
4. **Make `keyring` optional and feature-gated**, with graceful fallback on headless Linux/CI where Secret Service is absent (Claim 3).
5. **Seed runs with an empty commit** before opening the draft PR, since GitHub rejects PRs with zero commits between head and base (Claim 7).
6. **Reorder auth precedence to `GH_TOKEN > GITHUB_TOKEN > keyring > gh auth token > prompt`** and special-case Codespaces' restricted token (Claim 9).
7. **Detect push access and switch to fork-mode automatically** for contributors without upstream write; document that `dr/*` must not be branch-protected (Claim 8).

# Pre-Mortem & Wedge Review: deadreckon team-sync

## Setting

deadreckon is a deeply-built solo-first harness. README.md:7 frames the value — *"a harness around the agent CLI you already use, so you can actually walk away."* The shipped surface is large: signed `dr-gate` acceptance, sandboxed turn loop, durable per-turn snapshots, `attach`/`resume`/`undo`/`apply`/`abandon`/`extend`, autonomous `chain`s, self-documenting `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`/`RUN-AS-BUILT.md`/`RUN-DECISIONS.md` artifacts, and a promoted library at `~/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/` (AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1367–1398). The V1 backlog (V1-CANDIDATES.md) is a *single line* — sub-agent forking. AS-BUILT §22 lists "cloud sync of histories" and "real-time multi-cursor TUI presence" explicitly under **Not yet built** (AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1421–1423). MULTI-RUN.md is 13 lines: locks are scope-local, per-machine, file-system based — there is no notion of "another teammate" anywhere in the system today.

So team-sync would be a **first-of-its-kind cross-cutting feature** introduced into a codebase whose entire design discipline is local-first, file-on-disk, no daemons, no cloud. That asymmetry matters for what follows.

---

## PART A — Pre-mortem: why team-sync flops by Nov 2026

### 1. PR notification fatigue (Renovate/Dependabot precedent) — **HIGH**
Per-turn updates to a draft PR body produce a stream of `synchronize`/`edited` events. Even if the PR stays draft, every reviewer subscribed to the repo gets timeline churn. Renovate ships with an explicit dashboard issue *because* per-PR noise was unacceptable; Dependabot quietly added grouping for the same reason.
- **Failure mode:** within two weeks of adoption, repos disable the integration org-wide because the GitHub mobile app pings every commit.
- **Early signal:** GH issues titled `--no-auto-publish`, `please squash narrative updates`, "PR timeline shows 47 'updated description'."
- **Prevention:** *do not* update per turn. Publish at most twice — on first watchdog signoff and on `apply`. Or write to a single comment that gets edited in place (no timeline event) instead of the PR body.

### 2. Token / auth friction — **HIGH**
The proposal already hedges: `gh auth token` inheritance + OS keyring + env var. That's three auth paths, each with platform quirks (Linux keyring requires a session bus, macOS Keychain prompts the first time, Windows Credential Manager has its own scope rules), plus `gh` is not actually installed on a lot of CI/server boxes. Every additional token prompt is a churn cliff.
- **Failure mode:** doctor reports green; first `deadreckon publish` hangs on a keyring dialog inside a tmux pane and the user gives up.
- **Early signal:** silent drop-off between `init` runs and first successful `publish`; issues like "headless server: keyring D-Bus error."
- **Prevention:** prefer `gh` CLI subprocess over `octocrab` for the first version — it inherits whatever auth `gh` already has. Don't introduce `keyring` as a hard dep until there's a measured demand.

### 3. GitHub-only is too narrow — **MEDIUM**
deadreckon's sandbox layer already supports macOS *and* Linux (sandbox-exec, bwrap, docker, none). A GitHub-only sync layer breaks that platform-neutrality posture. GitLab, Gitea, Forgejo, Codeberg, and self-hosted Bitbucket together are not negligible; they over-index on the exact "auditable artifact" buyer deadreckon already targets (regulated industries, OSS-purist devs).
- **Failure mode:** the first three serious enterprise prospects say "we mirror to GitHub but our source of truth is GitLab, can't use this."
- **Early signal:** issue tracker fills with `gitlab support?` requests within a month.
- **Prevention:** design the artifact-publish surface as a `Forge` trait with GitHub as the first impl. But honestly — if you have to do that, you are building a forge-abstraction layer, which is a much bigger project than "GitHub team sync."

### 4. The user we designed for doesn't exist — **HIGH**
This is the most dangerous one. The README and DESIGN.md are about a *solo* developer who walks away from a long run. Chains (AS-BUILT §28) are explicitly "no cross-machine handoff, no cloud sync." There is no existing user research in the repo (no `docs/USERS.md`, no `docs/INTERVIEWS.md`, no telemetry; and the cited "five unmet team-collab needs" research isn't in the tree). The current alpha user is almost certainly: *one person, one laptop, often OSS, sometimes a contractor who hands a PR to a tiny team.*
- **Failure mode:** team-sync ships, and the actual deadreckon user — solo dev — sees more flags, more docs, more "do you want to publish?" prompts, and starts using `--no-publish` reflexively. The intended buyer (a 5-person team adopting deadreckon together) doesn't exist because no team has yet adopted deadreckon.
- **Early signal:** zero net-new team users in the first cohort; everyone toggling to `--no-publish`.
- **Prevention:** before building, find five teams currently running deadreckon. If you can't find them, you're building for a hypothesis. Defer.

### 5. Vendor lock-in / forge-agnostic drift — **MEDIUM**
Forgejo and Codeberg are growing precisely because of GitHub-fatigue. The audience that *most* values "auditable artifact, signed gate, evidence-not-trust" (deadreckon's pitch, README.md:31–35) overlaps heavily with the audience that's actively migrating *off* GitHub. Coupling deadreckon to GitHub asks them to walk back that decision.
- **Failure mode:** the loudest "I would buy this" voices are the ones GitHub-coupled most alienates.
- **Early signal:** Hacker News thread on the launch full of "why not just commit a markdown file and let me push it anywhere?"
- **Prevention:** see #3 — abstract the forge, or skip the forge entirely.

### 6. GitHub does it themselves — **MEDIUM-HIGH**
Copilot Workspace, "Coding Agent," and the agentic PR features are already shipping per-turn-style PR updates with built-in Check Runs and zero auth friction (it's just GitHub). By Nov 2026 GitHub's own integration will be deeper, free, and one click. A third-party tool that produces *the same artifact shape via the public API* loses on every axis except "model-agnostic" — and most teams don't pick tools on that axis.
- **Failure mode:** "we already have this in Copilot" closes every conversation.
- **Early signal:** GitHub ships an "agent run summary" surface at any GH Universe between now and ship.
- **Prevention:** *don't* compete on the artifact-in-PR axis. Compete on the axis GitHub structurally cannot — the *signed watchdog gate*, the *attach-from-anywhere durability*, the *agent-CLI-agnosticism*.

### 7. RUN-NARRATIVE.md schema staleness — **MEDIUM**
The doc set (RUN-NARRATIVE / RUN-AS-BUILT / RUN-DECISIONS / AS-BUILT-DELTA / `polish.json` v2 — AS-BUILT §22) is rich and recent. Once it's committed into squash bodies and indexed via `git notes`, schema changes are *immediate* breaking changes for every team that's already adopted the format. Agent-CLI churn is fast; this format will change.
- **Failure mode:** v0.4 changes the narrative schema; teams' historical apply commits become unparseable; angry issue.
- **Prevention:** version the artifacts (`RUN-NARRATIVE.md` front matter `schema: 2`), keep a separate machine-readable `manifest.json` as the API surface, and treat the narrative as human-readable prose only.

### 8. dr-gate Check Runs need a GitHub App — **HIGH for the OSS-solo user**
Posting Check Runs to a PR requires a GitHub App or Action token; a personal access token cannot create commit statuses on someone else's repo. Solo OSS contributors working *across* repos cannot install an org-wide app. So the `dr-gate` → Check Runs path *only works* in the team-with-org-admin setting, which is exactly the user we don't have.
- **Failure mode:** the most differentiated feature — proving the watchdog passed on the PR — only works if you control the repo's org settings.
- **Prevention:** post the gate result as a regular comment from the user's own account. Or as a status from a GitHub Action triggered by the `dr/...` push (see Wedge B4).

### 9. Per-turn API rate limits & noisy timeline — **MEDIUM**
Even ignoring notification fatigue, per-turn body edits chew through GitHub's *secondary* rate limits during long chains (a 6-step chain × 12 turns × body update = 72 edits per chain). Secondary limits are not documented and produce silent throttles.
- **Prevention:** publish on phase boundaries only (`provider`, `verify`, `complete`), not per turn.

### 10. Teams already have Linear/Slack/Notion — **HIGH**
A 5-person team already has a "where's the work" surface. Adding deadreckon's view on top creates two-source-of-truth confusion. The team won't migrate from Linear; they'll just stop using deadreckon's view.
- **Prevention:** don't build a view; build a paste-friendly summary that drops cleanly into the surfaces they already use (see Wedge B2).

---

## PART B — Alternative wedges

### B1. The "even smaller" wedge: just commit `.deadreckon/runs/`
`deadreckon apply` already builds a default commit body from the narrative (AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1382, DESIGN.md:106–109). The minimum viable team-sync is: commit the artifact directory into the repo on apply. Done. Zero network. Zero auth. Zero new deps. Reads like SpecStory's `.specstory/history/` pattern, which got real adoption precisely *because* it was a folder you could grep and gitignore — nothing more.
- **Target user:** any team using deadreckon, day one.
- **Adoption story:** "your runs become reviewable in the same diff your PR is in."
- **Why better:** every team-sync feature builds on this; nothing in #1–#10 above can fail because none of those moving parts exist.
- **Risk:** repo bloat. Mitigation: gitignore the heavy stuff (`snapshots/`, `traces.jsonl`), commit only the polished docs + manifest.

### B2. Markdown-to-clipboard
`deadreckon publish` produces a Markdown summary and copies to clipboard. User pastes into PR description, Slack, Linear, Notion, an email, an issue.
- **Target user:** the contractor/freelancer handing work back to a client team that *isn't* on deadreckon.
- **Adoption story:** "your run becomes a paragraph anyone can read, on any surface."
- **Why better:** no auth, no API quotas, no forge coupling, no notification fatigue. Works in CI. Works for GitLab teams. Works for the "we use Slack as the source of truth" team.
- **Risk:** feels too simple to charge for. (That's a feature for adoption, a problem for commercialization.)

### B3. MCP-server wedge
Expose runs over MCP so any IDE or agent CLI can introspect a teammate's runs. `deadreckon mcp serve` reads `~/.deadreckon/library/` and answers `list_runs`, `get_narrative`, `get_decisions`, `get_provenance`. Teammates point their Claude/Cursor at it.
- **Target user:** small team where everyone's already in an agentic IDE.
- **Adoption story:** "the agent your teammate is using *right now* can ask 'what did Greg's run on auth do yesterday?'"
- **Why better:** MCP is the rising substrate; one server replaces a forge integration *and* a query API *and* a chat-bot integration. AS-BUILT §22 already lists "MCP client surface" as a V1 candidate — this is the server-side mirror.
- **Risk:** MCP is still early; not every team's tool is an MCP host yet. Discovery is hard ("how do my teammates find my server?"). Best paired with B1.

### B4. GitHub Action wedge
Local CLI stays solo. Push to `dr/...` triggers a GitHub Action that runs `dr-gate`, posts a Check Run, and (optionally) opens a PR. The team substrate is CI, which teams already accept.
- **Target user:** any team whose convention is "code lands by way of CI."
- **Adoption story:** "your gate runs in the same place your tests run. No new auth."
- **Why better:** dodges failure modes #2 (auth), #8 (Check Run app), and #9 (rate limits — Actions can update statuses freely). The Action runs as `${{ github.token }}`, no PAT, no app install.
- **Risk:** GitHub-only; same blast radius as the original proposal for #3 and #5. But the surface area is *much* smaller (one Action, no client SDK), so porting to a GitLab CI variant is mechanical.

### B5. Watch-a-teammate's-repo (forge-agnostic index file)
A team-shared `.deadreckon/index.json` lives in *any* git repo. `deadreckon team subscribe <repo>` polls it. Forgejo, Gitea, GitLab, GitHub — anything that serves a file over git.
- **Target user:** the deadreckon-curious developer on Forgejo/Gitea who refuses to install GitHub.
- **Adoption story:** "team coordination via the file system you already share."
- **Risk:** discovery and concurrent-write coordination on the index file are non-trivial. But this rides exactly the current MULTI-RUN.md design philosophy (file locks, scope hashes) into the team space.

### B6. No team-sync; double down on solo
Sub-agent forking (the *only* item in V1-CANDIDATES.md), the watchdog gate as an end-user-visible commercial feature, sandbox profiles per project, real telemetry on adoption, MCP client (per AS-BUILT §22's V1 list), provider/cost-aware routing.
- **Target user:** the user who already exists.
- **Adoption story:** keep widening the moat where the moat actually is — *anti-self-attestation, sandboxing, run quality*.
- **Why better:** the entire pre-mortem section above evaporates. None of it can fail because none of it ships.
- **Risk:** real, not pretend — the "team layer" is where the money is in dev tools, and refusing to play means deferring revenue. But shipping a flop costs more.

---

## PART C — Recommendation: **Defer + Pivot to B1**

**Defer the GitHub-coupled team-sync as proposed.** It fails three independent acid tests:

1. **No validated user.** No teams currently using deadreckon-as-a-team are documented anywhere in the repo. Building for a hypothesized buyer is the most expensive mistake a 1-person project can make. (This is failure mode A.4, and it dominates everything else.)

2. **Asymmetric surface area.** The proposed wedge introduces `octocrab`, `keyring`, `secrecy`, `reqwest`, OAuth flows, GitHub App considerations, Check Run integrations, git notes — into a codebase whose North Star (DESIGN.md:7) is "intentionally local-first." That's a ~10× increase in cross-cutting concerns to serve a hypothetical user.

3. **Strategic exposure.** Failure modes A.1, A.6, A.8, A.9 are all *predictable today*. Shipping anyway means knowingly accepting them.

**Pivot to B1 as the actual next milestone.** The smallest possible "team-sync" is *change the default `apply` commit body to include the narrative, and add `--commit-runs` to also commit `.deadreckon/runs/<id>/` (filtered) into the squash*. That is a one-week change. It piggybacks on `apply`'s existing narrative-aware commit body (AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md:1382). It introduces zero new dependencies. It works on every forge. It alienates no one. And — critically — it lets you *measure* whether anyone actually wants the team layer before you build it: if zero PRs in the wild contain `.deadreckon/runs/`, then no one wanted team-sync. If some do, you have a real conversation with real users about what they want next.

**What the next goal+rider should target.** Build "committed run artifacts" as the team-sync wedge (B1). Ship `deadreckon apply --commit-runs` with sensible filtering (narrative + decisions + manifest + signed gate proof; *not* snapshots, traces, spend, history, or events). Add a `deadreckon publish --clipboard` (B2) as a complementary one-flag affordance for non-PR surfaces. Defer GitHub APIs, octocrab, keyring, Check Runs, and git-notes indexing to a later milestone *gated on observed demand* — specifically, on having three real teams who say "we tried committing the artifacts and now we want X." Keep the proposed GitHub wedge in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md` as a contingent plan, not an active build target. And treat sub-agent forking (the actual one-line item already in V1-CANDIDATES.md) as the higher-priority next thing on the solo-user spine, because it is *where the existing user is asking for more*.

The honest answer to "is GitHub-coupled the correct path forward?" is **no — not yet, and probably never in that shape**. Commit the artifact, paste the markdown, and let the demand pull the rest of the design out of the user.

# Survey: precedents for the deadreckon team-sync pattern

## 1. Direct precedents — agent runs published as PRs

| Tool | Pattern | Adoption signal | What worked / didn't |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GitHub Copilot Workspace** (original) | Issue-to-PR via spec-plan-implement pipeline | Sunset May 30 2025; rebuilt as "Copilot coding agent" | The Workspace UI flopped; the *underlying issue→draft-PR→commits-as-turns* pattern was kept and rebranded ([GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-meet-the-new-coding-agent/)) |
| **Copilot coding agent** | Assign issue to `@copilot`, agent pushes commits to a draft PR you can watch live | GA Sept 2025, available on Pro/Pro+/Business/Enterprise | Pricing complaints forced a "1 session = 1 premium request" rework — community wanted clearer cost per agent run ([GitHub Discussion #159068](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/159068)) |
| **Devin (Cognition)** | Opens its own PRs against your repo | 67% PR merge rate (up from 34%); priced reset from $500 → $20/mo (96% cut) in Apr 2025 to drive adoption ([VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/programming-development/devin-2-0-is-here-cognition-slashes-price-of-ai-software-engineer-to-20-per-month-from-500)) | Users complained about unpredictable failures and Devin "spending days on impossible solutions" ([Cognition 2025 review](https://cognition.ai/blog/devin-annual-performance-review-2025), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2025/01/23/ai_developer_devin_poor_reviews/)) |
| **Cursor BugBot / background agents** | Bot opens PRs / pushes commits to a branch from an event | 35% of Autofix changes merged; 76% pre-merge bug resolution rate (up from 52%) ([Cursor blog](https://cursor.com/blog/bugbot-autofix)) | The "auto-fix on a PR you already opened" framing reduced noise vs. pure bot-PR firehose |
| **OpenAI Codex web** | Cloud agent in `chatgpt.com/codex` opens PRs in parallel | Available to ChatGPT Plus since June 2025; ranked #1 coding agent in Apr 2026 refreshes ([Codex docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cloud)) | Strong adoption when bundled with an existing subscription; weak as standalone |
| **Jules (Google)** | Issue → reviewable PR with critic review pre-submission | "Significantly less community buzz and adoption compared to Devin or Claude Code" as of Mar 2026; being rebuilt as "Jitro" ([Nelson's log](https://nelsonslog.wordpress.com/2026/03/18/first-impressions-of-jules-googles-coding-agent/), [TestingCatalog](https://www.testingcatalog.com/google-prepares-jules-v2-agent-capable-of-taking-bigger-tasks/)) | Pure issue-to-PR without strong context loop didn't differentiate |
| **Sweep.dev** | The original "GitHub issue → PR" tool of 2024 | **Pivoted away from GitHub-bot PRs to a JetBrains plugin** (40k+ installs, v1.27 in Dec 2025) ([sweep.dev](https://sweep.dev/), [docs.sweep.dev/changelog](https://docs.sweep.dev/changelog)) | Their original pattern (the one we're proposing) was abandoned by the company that pioneered it. Sweep.io (CRM) is a different company ([Sweep.io](https://www.sweep.io/blog/sweep-io-vs-sweep-ai-what-s-the-difference)) |
| **Sourcegraph Amp** | Threads-as-shareable-URLs, server-stored, leaderboards | Active development; "thread maps", labels, search-by-thread-ID added 2026 ([Amp news](https://ampcode.com/news), [Amp manual](https://ampcode.com/manual)) | The shareable-URL pattern is winning over commit-everything-to-git for transcripts |
| **Aider** | Local CLI; commits per turn, no PR integration | `aider` ships a `.gitignore` with `.aider*` to *prevent* committing chat history ([Aider FAQ](https://aider.chat/docs/faq.html)) | Deliberately rejected the "transcripts in git" pattern |

**Backlash signal — bot PR fatigue is documented.** Renovate's whole pitch over Dependabot is grouping PRs because "logging in on Monday morning to find 50 separate PRs leads to alert fatigue, where developers simply close PRs without looking" ([nesbitt.io best practices](https://nesbitt.io/2026/01/10/16-best-practices-for-reducing-dependabot-noise.html), [Renovate docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/bot-comparison/)). Maintainer fatigue from agent-generated PRs is a named problem in 2026 — see the matplotlib incident where an agent published a "hit piece" after being rejected ([Fast Company](https://www.fastcompany.com/91492228/matplotlib-scott-shambaugh-opencla-ai-agent), [Socket.dev](https://socket.dev/blog/ai-agent-submits-pr-to-matplotlib-publishes-angry-blog-post-after-rejection)).

## 2. Run-artifact-in-git precedents

- **AGENTS.md** — adopted by 60,000+ repos; consolidated under the new Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation in Dec 2025 ([Linux Foundation press](https://www.linuxfoundation.org/press/linux-foundation-announces-the-formation-of-the-agentic-ai-foundation), [InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2025/08/agents-md/)). **Static config in git is a green light.**
- **`.cursor/rules/`** — committed widely; stable.
- **SpecStory `.specstory/history/`** — *transcripts* in git. Mixed reception: users have actively gitignored it because "everyone's files would be mixed in together"; the SpecStory team itself has a public discussion thread admitting the pattern needs work for teams ([SpecStory Discussion #48](https://github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/discussions/48)). Spec-Kit has the same debate ([spec-kit #1437](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/discussions/1437), [#769](https://github.com/github/spec-kit/discussions/769)).
- **Aider chat history** — *deliberately gitignored* by default. Aider auto-writes `.aider*` into `.gitignore` ([Aider FAQ](https://aider.chat/docs/faq.html)). The most established agentic-CLI in the field rejected this pattern.
- **Continue.dev** — *config* in git is encouraged (`.continue/` dirs); transcripts/sessions go through Hub Configurations because committing them mixes API keys and creates churn ([Continue docs](https://docs.continue.dev/customize/deep-dives/configuration), [understanding-configs](https://docs.continue.dev/guides/understanding-configs)).
- **Sourcegraph Amp threads** — explicitly *not* in git; stored on Sourcegraph servers with shareable URLs ([Amp manual](https://ampcode.com/manual)).
- **OpenTelemetry GenAI traces** — invariably shipped to an observability backend, not committed.

**Pattern:** static config (AGENTS.md, .cursor/rules) wins in git; *per-turn transcripts* are either gitignored (Aider) or routed to a server (Amp, Continue Hub). SpecStory is the closest precedent for our pattern, and it's actively wrestling with the team-coordination cost.

## 3. Git notes reality check

The good news: notes work and are still in use. Gerrit's `refs/notes/review` continues to attach review metadata in production ([Gerrit reviewnotes](https://gerrit.googlesource.com/plugins/reviewnotes/+/refs/heads/master/src/main/resources/Documentation/refs-notes-review.md)). A 2025 tool, [git-ai](https://github.com/git-ai-project/git-ai), uses notes to track AI-attributed commits — direct precedent for our use case.

The bad news: **GitHub stopped rendering commit notes in 2014 and has not changed** ([Tyler Cipriani](https://tylercipriani.com/blog/2022/11/19/git-notes-gits-coolest-most-unloved-feature/)). Google's `git-appraise` (the most ambitious notes-based system) has had the same "Open" issues sitting for years — it works but never crossed the chasm ([git-appraise](https://github.com/google/git-appraise), [HN 2023](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=37084575)). Notes also require explicit `git fetch refs/notes/*:refs/notes/*` to share — a known UX cliff.

**Verdict:** notes are a viable *substrate* for tooling that pulls them programmatically, not a viable *UX surface* for humans browsing on github.com. Use them only if our UI never assumes the user can see them in a web view.

## 4. Check Runs vs commit statuses for non-App CLIs

This is unambiguous and load-bearing for `dr-gate`:

> **Write permission for the Check Runs REST API is only available to GitHub Apps.** OAuth apps and authenticated users can view check runs but cannot create them ([GitHub REST docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs), [Ken Muse](https://www.kenmuse.com/blog/creating-github-checks/)).

The standard workaround when you don't want to ship a GitHub App: use the **commit status API** instead. Personal access tokens and `gh auth token` can write commit statuses freely. Cargo's release tooling and most CI integrations that don't ship as Apps default to statuses for exactly this reason. If `dr-gate` must show as a Check Run, it needs either (a) a real GitHub App with installation tokens, or (b) to run inside GitHub Actions where `GITHUB_TOKEN` has check-write scope by default ([authenticate-with-github_token](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/authenticate-with-github_token)).

## 5. Auth-via-`gh` precedent

This pattern is real and well-precedented in Rust:

- The `gh-token` crate exists specifically to deserialize GitHub CLI's token from `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` for Rust consumers ([lib.rs/gh-token](https://lib.rs/crates/gh-token)).
- `gh-config` provides the same functionality as a hybrid library/CLI ([crates.io/gh-config](https://crates.io/crates/gh-config)).
- `cargo-binstall` already attempts to retrieve tokens from `gh auth token` and git credential helpers as part of its auto-discovery ([cargo-binstall #1681](https://github.com/cargo-bins/cargo-binstall/issues/1681)).
- `release-plz` accepts `GITHUB_TOKEN` env var and is the standard recommendation for Rust release automation ([release-plz quickstart](https://release-plz.dev/docs/github/quickstart)).
- `gh auth token` is officially documented as a programmatic interface to extract the token ([gh docs](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_auth_token)), and GitHub recommends it as a `git credential.helper` ([cli/cli #5081](https://github.com/cli/cli/discussions/5081)).

**Verdict: green light.** Inheriting from `gh auth token` is a normal Rust-CLI pattern with multiple production precedents.

## 6. Solo→team CLI evolution patterns

The empirical record:

- **Atuin** (200k+ devs) — went solo→team carefully, encrypted client-side, "exploring what happens when their open-source philosophy meets team workflows" ([Atuin home](https://atuin.sh/), [Changelog #579](https://changelog.com/podcast/579)). Team features added *after* solo product-market fit was clear.
- **Fig** — added Scripts/Dotfiles/Plugins/SSH-sharing as team features, got acquired by Amazon, **and all those team features were killed** in the migration to Amazon Q ([fig sunset](https://fig.io/blog/post/fig-is-sunsetting), [AWS docs](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/devops/exploring-the-latest-features-of-the-amazon-q-developer-cli/)). The team stuff was the *first* thing to go.
- **Warp** — heavy team features tied to a $20/mo paywall; sustained Hacker News backlash about "paying for a terminal," with the most common comparison being "for $20 I could just buy Claude Code" ([HN 45772558](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45772558), [BigGo](https://finance.biggo.com/news/202510312004_Warp-Terminal-New-Pricing-Debate)).
- **Sapling (Meta)** — open-sourced client, but the server (Mononoke) stayed proprietary; near-zero adoption outside Meta ([Medium analysis](https://medium.com/@benneighbour/is-metas-sapling-the-future-of-vcs-3d106fcebce0)). Team features that depend on a server you can't run = dead on arrival.
- **lazygit** — stayed solo; no team-feature attempt; thriving.

**Pattern for success:** (1) nail solo first (Atuin), (2) team features are *opt-in and use existing substrates the user already has* (git remote, GitHub auth) rather than a new server, (3) avoid paywalling the team layer if the solo product was free (Warp's lesson). **Pattern for failure:** require a new server (Sapling/Mononoke), or bolt team features on as a monetization wedge (Warp, Fig pre-acquisition).

## 7. Verdict for each load-bearing pattern

| Pattern | Light | One-sentence reason |
|---|---|---|
| Auto-publish runs as draft PRs that update per turn | **Yellow** | Copilot coding agent and Cursor BugBot prove the UX works, but Sweep.dev abandoned this exact pattern and bot-PR fatigue is documented. |
| Commit `.deadreckon/runs/<id>/` artifact bundles | **Yellow→Red** | SpecStory's wrestling and Aider's deliberate gitignore both signal this is the friction-heavy choice; static config is fine, transcripts are not. |
| `dr-gate` as GitHub Check Runs | **Red** without a GitHub App | The Checks write API is App-only; CLI tools that aren't Apps must use commit statuses instead. |
| Git notes for team index | **Yellow** | Works as a tooling substrate (Gerrit, git-ai prove it), invisible on github.com web UI — only viable if our reader never assumes browser visibility. |
| Auth via `gh auth token` inheritance | **Green** | Standard pattern with multiple Rust crates (`gh-token`, `gh-config`) and tools (`cargo-binstall`) already doing it. |

## Five precedents we should explicitly mimic

1. **Copilot coding agent's "draft PR that updates per turn"** — the live-commits-as-turns metaphor is the proven UX ([GitHub Blog](https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-meet-the-new-coding-agent/)).
2. **AGENTS.md as the in-repo agent contract** — 60k+ repos, now an LF standard; piggyback on it rather than inventing new files ([agents.md](https://agents.md/)).
3. **Renovate's grouping/`prHourlyLimit`** — the canonical answer to bot-PR fatigue; default to one PR per logical unit, not one per turn ([Renovate docs](https://docs.renovatebot.com/bot-comparison/)).
4. **`gh auth token` + `gh-token` crate** — proven Rust-CLI auth inheritance, no new credential surface ([lib.rs/gh-token](https://lib.rs/crates/gh-token)).
5. **Sourcegraph Amp's shareable thread URLs** — server-side thread store with a stable URL is winning over git-committed transcripts; consider this even if we still write to git ([Amp manual](https://ampcode.com/manual)).

## Three precedents we should explicitly avoid

1. **Sweep.dev's original "GitHub-issue-to-PR-bot" architecture** — the company that invented our exact pattern *pivoted away from it* to a JetBrains plugin ([sweep.dev](https://sweep.dev/)). That's the loudest signal in this report.
2. **GitHub Check Runs from a non-App CLI** — the API simply will not let you write checks without an App; building toward it is wasted engineering ([GitHub Checks REST docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs)).
3. **Sapling/Mononoke's "team features need our server" trap** — any pattern that requires a deadreckon-hosted backend will replicate Sapling's near-zero external adoption ([Sapling analysis](https://medium.com/@benneighbour/is-metas-sapling-the-future-of-vcs-3d106fcebce0)).

# Verdict: the proposed GitHub-coupled design fails its own stress test

Three of the four agents independently arrive at the same recommendation: **defer the GitHub-coupled team-sync as proposed; pivot to a much smaller "commit the artifact" wedge.** The technical agent breaks specific load-bearing claims; the precedent agent finds the killer counter-example; the adoption agent finds no evidence of the user we'd be building for; the adversarial agent enumerates ten plausible failure modes and recommends defer + pivot.

I'm going to say this plainly: **my prior "elegant solution" answer was substantially wrong.** Here's what broke, what survives, and what to actually do.

## What broke

| Claim I made | What the evidence says |
|---|---|
| `dr-gate` posts to GitHub **Check Runs** | **Killed.** Check Runs write API is GitHub-Apps-only. PATs and OAuth tokens cannot create check runs ([GitHub REST docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/checks/runs), [community #129512](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/129512)). The elegant story collapses unless we ship and operate a GitHub App — a different distribution model entirely. |
| **Git notes** as the team registry | **Killed for UX.** GitHub stopped rendering notes in 2014; they don't appear in any UI users browse ([Tyler Cipriani](https://tylercipriani.com/blog/2022/11/19/git-notes-gits-coolest-most-unloved-feature/)). They work as a tooling substrate (Gerrit, git-ai) but not as a discovery surface. |
| **Per-turn draft-PR body updates** as the live coordination object | **Bad idea.** Hits GitHub's 500/hr secondary content-creation limit on chatty runs and creates Renovate/Dependabot-style notification fatigue (well-documented; matplotlib incident). |
| **Auto-publish on first run** | **Reverses deadreckon's own narrative.** README's pitch is *"isolated worktree, your checkout never touched."* Asking on first run "publish to a remote?" is whiplash. |
| **The target user** ("Alice/Bob/Carol on three different agents") | **Aspirational.** Not in README, DESIGN.md, HOWTO, AS-BUILT, or V1-CANDIDATES. The actual current user is the senior solo dev who walks away from a long run. |
| **Copilot Workspace as positive precedent** | **Inverted.** GitHub itself sunset the "agent run = draft PR" UX in May 2025. Sweep.dev pioneered the same pattern in 2024 and **pivoted away from it** to a JetBrains plugin. The two strongest precedents both walked back from this design. |

## What survives

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **`octocrab` is the right Rust GitHub client** | Confirmed. v0.50.0, active, GraphQL + REST + GitHub App auth. |
| **`gh auth token` inheritance** | Confirmed and well-precedented in Rust (`gh-token`, `gh-config` crates; `cargo-binstall` does it). Order should be `GH_TOKEN > GITHUB_TOKEN > keyring > gh > prompt`. |
| **Commit the run artifact into `.deadreckon/runs/`** | Survives — but barely. Aider deliberately gitignores chat history; SpecStory's team is publicly wrestling with the same pattern. The version that survives is **narrative + decisions + manifest + gate-proof only**, not full traces / snapshots / events. |
| **Solo users see zero behavior change** | Confirmed mechanically — `git remote -v` parsing, hard-gate every team path on `is_github && has_token`. |
| **AGENTS.md adoption** | Confirmed — 60k+ repos, Linux Foundation Agentic AI Foundation. Static config in git is a green light. |

## Adoption assessment

The adoption thesis I should have written:

> **Solo CLIs that successfully add team features (Atuin) do so by extending substrates the user already has (existing remote, existing auth) without requiring a new server. Solo CLIs that fail (Sapling, Fig's team features, Warp's premium tier) require a server, a paywall, or both. The most successful CLI in deadreckon's neighborhood — Aider, 39k stars / 4M installs — has _no_ PR integration and explicitly _gitignores_ its chat history. The agent-run-as-PR pattern was attempted by GitHub itself (Copilot Workspace) and Sweep.dev and abandoned by both.**

The honest read: **building "Alice + Bob + Carol on three agents" before any team is documented as using deadreckon is building for a hypothesized user.** The single line in V1-CANDIDATES.md is `deadreckon fork` — the existing-user ask is more sub-agent control, not team coordination.

## Recommended path forward

**Defer the PR/Checks/notes design entirely.** Pivot to the sequence below.

### Step 1 — Ship "artifact in commit" (the B1 / Option-S wedge)

This is the only piece of the original synthesis that survives every agent's scrutiny:

- `deadreckon apply` already builds a default commit body from the narrative.
- Add `--commit-runs` (or make it default-on with `--no-commit-runs` to opt out): write a curated subset to `.deadreckon/runs/<run-id>/` in the squash commit:
  - `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, `manifest.json`, `acceptance.json` (the gate proof)
  - `failed-attempts.md` distilled from events.jsonl — the highest-value missing-from-everywhere artifact per the external research
  - **Not** snapshots, traces.jsonl, spend.jsonl, full events.jsonl. Those stay machine-local. Gitignore template included.
- Add `state.created_by` (`$USER` + `git config user.email` + provider/model) — the missing identity primitive everything else would depend on.
- Zero new dependencies. No `octocrab`. No `keyring`. No GitHub auth. Works on every forge.

This is one rider, ~11 phases, zero behavior change for users who don't pass the flag. It's the SpecStory-precedent move with deadreckon's much richer artifact set.

### Step 2 — Add `deadreckon publish --clipboard` (the B2 wedge)

Markdown summary to clipboard. Pasteable into any PR description, Slack, Linear, Notion, email, or issue. No auth, no API, no infra. One flag. Probably one phase of a small rider.

### Step 3 — Stop and measure before building anything else

Before any `octocrab`, GitHub App, draft-PR integration, or Action wedge: look for actual usage signal. Are people committing `.deadreckon/runs/` into PRs? Are multiple users appearing in `state.created_by` on the same repo? If yes, the team layer is real and the next rider can target it. If not, the V1 list (sub-agent forking) is the honest next priority — *that's where the existing user is asking for more*.

### What stays in V1-CANDIDATES (don't preempt)

- Auto-publish draft PRs / per-turn PR body updates
- `dr-gate` Check Runs (requires shipping a GitHub App)
- Git notes index
- `octocrab` integration of any kind
- Cross-machine resume / approval workflows / team registry

These should be logged in `V1-CANDIDATES.md` with the **specific evidence threshold** that would justify building them (e.g., "build the Check Runs path only after three teams have requested it AND we've decided to ship a deadreckon GitHub App").

## What I'd want before drafting the goal

Two questions worth answering before the next goal+rider:

1. **Is `--commit-runs` default-on or default-off?** Default-on means every `apply` lands a `.deadreckon/runs/` directory in the user's repo. Reviewers might love or hate this depending on size. Default-off means low adoption but zero blast radius. I lean default-off with a one-line preflight hint ("`try: deadreckon apply --commit-runs` to share this run with your team") — matches deadreckon's existing friendliness pattern.

2. **Should this rider also do `failed-attempts.md` distillation, or is that a separate rider?** It's the single highest-value handoff artifact per the external research and it's nearly free given what `events.jsonl` already records — but it's a real piece of work (distillation logic, formatting, a new section in `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`). If kept in scope, the rider is heavier; if split out, the wedge ships sooner.

Once you answer those, I'd draft `2026-05-12-<HHMM>-deadreckon-share-{goal,rider}.md` (headline word: probably **Share** — emphasizing artifact, not infrastructure). The work is small, defensible, and pulls in zero of the rejected design's failure modes.

The original "elegant GitHub-coupled" answer optimized for cleverness over evidence. The honest path forward is the un-clever one: commit the file, let demand pull the rest.
